# Daily-driving limiter findings

### L003 — Checkpoint capture inherits patch byte ceilings

- `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench/checkpoints/capture.rs:246-254` reads each whole file with `peritus_patch::MAX_FILE_BYTES`, then maps **every** inspection error to `ControlError::StaleRevision`.
- Selected checkpoint capture also rejects aggregate body bytes above `peritus_patch::MAX_PATCH_BYTES` at lines 53-62; checkpoint recapture does the same at lines 79-88.
- Daily-driving blocker: checkpoints of ordinary build artifacts can fail before a command runs. The per-file bound was implicated by the prior live-run diagnosis. Exact constant definitions, automatic command caller, persistence format, and restore enforcement will be verified by complete reads in this audit.
- Structural issue: patch payload admission limits are reused as checkpoint file/storage limits, and capacity/I/O failures become a revision-change error. Merely increasing a number would leave that coupling and misleading error path intact.
- Exact byte declarations are now read in `peritus-patch/src/set.rs:11-16`: both `MAX_FILE_BYTES` and `MAX_PATCH_BYTES` are **8 MiB**. Automatic capture at `checkpoints/capture/automatic.rs:71-75` calls the same capped `observe_path`; manual capture at `checkpoints.rs:148` does too. Sealing a manual checkpoint recaptures every path at `automatic.rs:152-169`, and fork validation at `checkpoints.rs:68-78` likewise recaptures paths.
- `product_run/interaction/live.rs:118-142` now verifies the live workspace-mutation hook: automatic capture failure returns an error stating that Peritus did not change the workspace. Sealing failures also stop with a durable-recording error. `peritus-product-runner/src/execution/checkpoint.rs:89-133` now verifies the observer forwards BeforeMutation to that ConversationView hook; `turn.rs:280-291` installs it on writer/fixer tools, and `executor.rs:243-257` rejects failed preflight before dispatch. The live precommand capture chain is source-verified. Durable storage and restore have been read and add independent ceilings (L013, L020, L021).

### L004 — Checkpoint coverage omits partial selections and empty directories

- `capture.rs:30-50` excludes deselected files, external imports without a workspace path, partial file ranges, folder-identity mismatches, and duplicate references from selected restore coverage.
- Lines 190-226 record an empty-directory exclusion because an automatic checkpoint cannot restore the directory; the directory must be empty when observed.
- Daily-driving effect: whole-file capture and directory restoration are distinct capabilities. A selected range cannot become a whole-file restore point under this implementation, and removed empty directories lack restoration coverage. Callers and recovery behavior remain pending.
- `checkpoints.rs:42-45` explicitly excludes credentials, approvals, process state, and external side effects while preserving conversation/goal/accounting history. Lines 65-69 allow a read-only fork without captured-path validation but reject a writable fork with no checkpoint paths.

### L006 — Patch creation, replacement, deletion, and encoding admission limits

- `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/set.rs:11-16,40-60` declares **8 MiB per file**, **8 MiB aggregate final payload**, and **1,024 operations**. Any present preimage above 8 MiB is rejected, including a delete operation with no final bytes. `content.rs:31-39` rejects transformed final bytes above 8 MiB.
- `verified.rs:19-32` requires a nonempty patch and enforces both operation count and final-byte totals. `set.rs:158-196` canonicalizes through `CodecLimits::PRODUCTION`; encoder errors collapse to a generic patch-bounds error. `set.rs:88` additionally requires transaction-manifest capacity.
- Daily-driving effect: ordinary large files cannot be edited or deleted through this patch representation; a sufficiently large multi-file change cannot be admitted as one patch. The production codec and transaction-manifest bounds may further restrict payloads; those definitions/callers are pending complete reads.

### L007 — Independent source-scan and included-content ceilings

- `crates/runtime/peritus-workspace/src/scoped_inspection.rs:16-17` caps the **complete source at 64 MiB**. `scoped_inspection/read.rs:98-109` rejects it before scanning even for a small selected range.
- `inspection.rs:9-10` caps **included content at 8 MiB**. `scoped_inspection/read.rs:30-32` refuses a zero or larger caller bound; whole files and selected ranges are rejected rather than truncated at lines 101-109 and 134-138.
- `scoped_inspection/selection.rs:26-38` rejects byte ranges beyond 64 MiB and line selections beyond **67,108,864** lines. Full source hashing and metadata checks are coupled to range reads, so selecting fewer bytes cannot bypass the source cap.
- Daily-driving effect: inspection/attachment/checkpoint callers can refuse ordinary large build artifacts and datasets. Checkpoint capture supplies the full-file 8 MiB bound (L003); remaining callers are pending.

### L008 — Path representation and all-or-nothing directory inspection

- `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/path.rs:7-12,27-49,84-105` limits components to **255 UTF-8 bytes**, paths to **4,096 bytes**, and depth to **256 components**. The actual path/depth predicate repeats literal values in `verified.rs:9-15`.
- The path schema also rejects noncanonical/traversal paths, control characters, backslashes, colons, trailing dots/spaces, Windows device names on every platform, and protected Git/Peritus metadata. Traversal/protected-path checks are authority boundaries; portability and representational ceilings have separate daily-driving consequences.
- `peritus-workspace/src/inspection.rs:109-124,161-171` rejects an entire directory listing when one child name is non-UTF-8/nonrepresentable or one child is a symlink/special node. This file skips protected metadata, but does not skip or report individual unsupported ordinary entries.
- Daily-driving effect: an otherwise usable Unix folder can become unlistable because a single child is outside this portable schema. More directory/tool callers and error presentation remain pending.

### L009 — Canonical codec production ceilings

- `crates/foundation/peritus-codec/src/limits.rs:20-29,52-55` makes production limits the default: **16 MiB complete frame**, payload **16 MiB minus frame header**, **65,535 collection items**, **1 MiB per UTF-8 string**, **8 MiB per opaque field**, and **64 nested aggregates**.
- `writer.rs:87-125,128-150` rejects opaque/string/collection/depth/total-payload excess before writing. `reader.rs:106-157` independently rejects opaque/string/collection/depth excess on decode. Length prefixes use `u32` representation; these structural representation bounds differ from the configured smaller ceilings.
- Daily-driving effect depends on each caller's chosen limits and whether a representation contains a whole file, growing conversation, or transient message. Patch identity already uses these production limits (L006). Frame/message enforcement and remaining callers are pending.

### L010 — Checkpoint manifest count and text-field ceilings

- `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/checkpoint.rs:114,156-160,178-182,313-319` limits each path/exclusion/external-effect vector through `u16` conversion (**65,535 entries**). Field types are `ControlText<4096>` for paths, `<256>` for names, and `<512>` for exclusions/external effects; `control/text.rs:20-25,36-39` enforces the byte ceiling on construction and deserialization.
- `checkpoint/restore.rs:31,132-138` applies a 65,535 conflict-path count and `ControlText<4096>` path text; invalid settlement/count combinations return `InvalidInput`.
- Potential cross-type blocker: automatic empty-directory capture places a path plus explanation in a 512-byte exclusion field while accepting paths up to 4,096 bytes (L004/L008). The ControlText byte check is verified. This is a source-established admission mismatch; an executable reproduction has not yet been run.
- Ownership/run/revision/idempotency checks are recorded separately from count/byte ceilings; file bodies are explicitly separate artifacts, not manifest fields.

### L011 — Durable control and request-context size admission

- `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control.rs:62-68` binds maximum control-operation/current-state bytes to `peritus_journal::MAX_STATE_BYTES`, and combined request-context bytes to `ProtocolLimits::PRODUCTION.max_text_bytes()`. `peritus-journal/src/record/state.rs:8-11,87-99` defines and enforces **16 MiB per durable state value** and **1,024 bytes per state key**; the request-context text value is **16 MiB** in `peritus-model-protocol/src/bounds.rs:32`. Growing-state serialization enforcement is still being traced.
- Its public errors at lines 91-99 describe `StaleRevision` as “control state changed; refresh and reapply the exact intent,” and `Capacity` as “control state capacity exceeded.” This confirms the misleading user-visible wording reached by checkpoint inspection error collapse (L003).
- The schema is explicitly versioned; unsupported persisted generations are rejected. Migration/recovery behavior remains pending.

### L012 — Derived text can exceed otherwise valid field capacity

- `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/text.rs:20-25` rejects a string above its const byte ceiling. There is no truncation or overflow accommodation.
- Automatic empty-directory checkpoint exclusions concatenate an otherwise accepted path and explanatory text before storing it in `ControlText<512>` (L010). A sufficiently long valid path therefore fails automatic checkpoint admission.
- `peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench/checkpoints/logical.rs:34-37` prefixes an existing conversation title with `Rewind of `, then applies `ConversationTitle::new`; its failure becomes `ControlError::Capacity`. Exact title ceiling and public callers are pending.
- Structural issue: transformations enlarge already-admitted values while reusing the original destination ceiling. This can block recovery/branching because of incidental label length.

### L013 — Checkpoint coverage and restore capabilities disagree

- `checkpoints/rewind/plan.rs:29-73` creates one PatchOperation per changed Restore path and constructs bounded `FinalFile`/`PatchSet` values. Checkpoint admission allows 65,535 paths (L010), while patch admission accepts only 1,024 operations and 8 MiB of final bytes (L006).
- A manual checkpoint of more than 1,024 small files can fit its capture limits, but restoring all those files in one rewind exceeds patch operation admission. This conclusion follows from the fully read implementations; executable reproduction is pending.
- `checkpoints/projection.rs:152-154` collapses every PatchError into `InvalidInput`, discarding the actual byte/count/recovery classification. Preview and apply also re-read current files through L003's capped capture path.
- Required structural repair must align capture, durable representation, restore execution, and recovery capability; changing the capture ceiling alone would leave an unrestorable checkpoint path.

### L014 — RecoveryRequired restore can become a persistent recovery barrier

- `checkpoints/rewind.rs:60-65` refuses every new rewind preview if any prior restore is Prepared or RecoveryRequired, including a conversation-only preview.
- `checkpoints/recovery.rs:68-75,104-120` discards plan reconstruction, C1 reconciliation, and checkpoint inspection errors. Missing/uncertain evidence yields RecoveryRequired at lines 125-151 and 197-229.
- `checkpoints/lookup.rs:105-157` reconciles only Prepared records; an existing RecoveryRequired record takes the terminal receipt path instead. `control/checkpoint/restore.rs:129-136` only permits settlement from Prepared, and `control/record/transition/checkpoint.rs:127-139` calls that same transition.
- Daily-driving consequence: a transient capacity/I/O/inspection failure during recovery can produce a durable state that blocks subsequent rewind attempts and is not retried by the inspected recovery entrypoint. Whether another explicit repair path exists elsewhere remains pending whole-codebase coverage.
- Exact preimage/postimage and ownership evidence are real recovery constraints; the concern is loss of the error cause and terminal classification of unresolved recovery.

### L015 — Workspace run admission, folder mode, and result pagination

- `peritus-daemon/src/product_run.rs:159-177` rejects duplicate run IDs, an existing active run in the same workspace, and any workspace barrier enforced by deliverable discard. The active-run predicate and discard implementation are pending full reads.
- Lines 241-245 reject Build mode for a registered ordinary folder with GitRequired. This is a mode/workspace capability restriction, not an elapsed deadline.
- Lines 262-265 cap each run-list page at `MAX_PRODUCT_RUN_PAGE` and support an offset. Pagination alone does not prove lost records or stopped work; its definition/callers remain pending.
- Provider fallbacks at lines 289-298 are populated only when automatic provider failover is configured.

### L017 — Model protocol hard ceilings cannot be widened by profiles

- `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/bounds.rs:29-43` declares: **4,096 messages**, **16,384 content blocks**, **16 MiB text**, **32 MiB per inline media value**, **128 MiB aggregate inline media**, **1,024 tools**, **2 MiB schema**, **1,000,000 events**, **65,536 response items**, **8 MiB per event**, **256 MiB assembled output**, **16 MiB tool arguments**, and **2 MiB provider extension**.
- `ProtocolLimits::new` at lines 50-59 rejects zero and any value above production. Provider profiles can only narrow these ceilings; a user cannot request a wider value through this constructor.
- Daily-driving effect depends on request construction, stream reducers, provider profiles, and whether cumulative retained context crosses these bounds. Request count/capability enforcement, nested JSON bounds and canonical encoding are now fully read in L457-L460; provider and higher-level caller coverage remains tracked individually. `control.rs` already uses the 16 MiB text value for combined request-context admission (L011).

### L018 — Journal causal-parent, frame, and global-query bounds

- `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/record.rs:14-15,55-56,141-147` declares **4,096 records per global query window** and enforces **4,096 causal parents per event**. ExactFrame construction at lines 74-81 validates production codec framing (L009).
- Retention-gap reporting at lines 48-52 compares the caller's next position with the earliest retained position. This declaration does not establish whether events are actually deleted or whether a consumer fails to page; journal options/query/retention callers remain pending.

### L016 — Transaction manifest ancestor and decoder ceilings

- `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/transaction/manifest.rs:227-244` expands every operation into every ancestor path before validating manifest capacity. This includes ancestors that already exist, not just directories that a transaction will create.
- Encoding at lines 121-147 uses L009's production codec: a created-directory collection cannot exceed **65,535** and total manifest payload must fit **16 MiB minus header**, including its checksum. Thus paths/operations within L006/L008 can still fail admission due to expanded ancestor representation.
- Decoding at lines 150-173 and 260-269 re-enforces payload capacity, **1,024 entries**, and **8 MiB file identities**. Decode failure becomes `CorruptManifest` with `FenceWorkspace` at lines 303-310.
- Structural consequence: admission, stored manifest, recovery reader, and expanded ancestor representation all carry the same hard policies. Raising only one limit would leave other rejection/fencing paths intact.

### L019 — Control journal has a 250 ms lock-wait deadline

- `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_control/storage.rs:65-80` obtains an exclusive ownership lock immediately with `try_lock`, then opens SQLite with `busy_timeout = Duration::from_millis(250)`.
- **250 ms** is an explicit artificial database lock-wait deadline. `peritus-journal/src/sqlite/connection.rs:242-245` applies the supplied timeout directly through rusqlite. The same adapter has a separate **5-second default** at lines 17-20. Retry callers remain pending full reads; no inference is made yet about which live operation encountered it.
- The ownership lock is a separate exclusive-writer constraint. Its Drop implementation explicitly releases ownership after journal close (lines 48-60), preserving inherited-handle behavior.
- `product_control/error.rs:42-55` preserves typed sources internally, while public Journal failures say reconciliation is required and I/O failures conflate unavailable storage with existing ownership. A transient busy deadline may therefore be presented as a durable integrity/availability issue; adapter classification remains pending.

### L020 — Journal atomic-batch ceilings restrict checkpoint admission

- `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/append_plan.rs:17-28` declares **4,096 events**, **1,024 aggregate heads**, **4,096 state installs**, **4,096 outbox rows**, **4,096 outbox acknowledgements**, and **4,096 artifact dependencies** per atomic batch. `plan` calls bound validation at lines 131-138; `append_plan/validation.rs:17-39` enforces every listed count bound.
- `product_control/storage/checkpoints.rs:214-240` creates one StateInstall per present checkpoint body. `product_control/storage.rs:207-235` adds a conversation-root state and receipt state to that same batch. This creates another admission layer beneath L010's 65,535-path manifest bound.
- Checkpoint keys additionally cast their path index to `u16` at `storage/checkpoints.rs:243-247`.
- Daily-driving effect: a many-file checkpoint can fit its manifest and byte limits while exceeding the atomic state-install count. The fully read validation helper confirms rejection. More than **4,094 present bodies** exceeds the 4,096-install cap after the root and receipt installs are added. Executable reproduction is pending.

### L021 — Every ordinary control read re-verifies the entire growing archive

- `product_control/storage/replay.rs:14-75` implements current and historical conversation reads by loading the complete current aggregate, replaying every operation, and comparing the reconstructed state root. Each historical read still verifies the full current archive.
- For each operation, lines 78-140 verify associated request/file/checkpoint/image/reply archives. `storage/checkpoints.rs:165-210` rereads and hashes every retained before-image for that checkpoint operation. `storage.rs:186-214` performs replay before each new transition and serializes the entire successor ConversationRecord into one capped state value (L011).
- This is an algorithmic daily-driving risk independent of elapsed deadlines: work per ordinary read/mutation grows with all historical events and retained artifact bytes. The inspected implementation does not use a verified incremental replay cursor or a bounded append-only projection checkpoint here.
- The journal aggregate query, conversation replay implementation, locking/presentation callers, and actual production scaling behavior remain pending; no benchmark or live lockup is attributed solely to this source finding.

### L023 — Synchronous global control ownership and run-state publication barriers

- `product_run/workbench.rs:298-321` holds one synchronous mutex for the whole ControlStore operation across every conversation. Current workbench queries at lines 229-245 call full replay directly; the async command path also performs synchronous control work at lines 157-175.
- `product_run/execution.rs:22-103,106-151,340-347` holds the run registry's write lock across observation/finish work, durable persistence, checkpoint sealing, goal settlement, and reply publication. This can compose L021's full-history/file verification with blocking state/owner locks.
- `execution.rs:25-27,113-115` drops future updates/terminal processing for a run already marked RecoveryRequired. Failed checkpoint sealing at line 133 and several persist_record calls discard the concrete error; public-reply publication failure sets persistence_failed and fails handoff.
- Daily-driving effect: growing replay or storage work can delay unrelated UI queries/controls even without an elapsed timeout, and some failure causes are hidden. Lock order across other callers and recovery of the frozen state remain pending; no deadlock is asserted from this file alone.
- `execution/launch.rs:96-112` explicitly sets ordinary-run `max_elapsed: None` and supplies retained resume/live-conversation handles. Its goal-clock wrapper and task recovery are separate pending paths.

### L024 — SQLite native length and configurable database page ceilings

- `peritus-journal/src/sqlite/connection.rs:268-273` sets `SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH` to **32 MiB** and attached-database count to **zero**. The length limit is an additional hard database representation ceiling; attached-database restriction is a connection-security boundary.
- `connection.rs:173-204` exposes `limit_storage_pages`, rejects zero/unrepresentable/below-current ceilings, and sets `max_page_count`; transactions requiring another page then fail with SQLITE_FULL. The method does not lower storage by deleting existing pages.
- Default page-budget callers and real disk-pressure handling remain pending. A configurable page limit is not evidence that the default daemon imposes a small database quota; only the API/enforcement is established here.
- Schema/store identity and WAL activation are admission requirements at lines 99-113,246-255,277-350. Unsupported generations require the migration owner rather than implicit reset.

### L025 — Public activity windows and text truncation

- `peritus-daemon/src/product_run/interaction.rs:106-127,138-231,357-365` truncates activity text/detail to the imported `MAX_PRODUCT_ACTIVITY_BYTES`, chunks streamed text to that ceiling, and removes the oldest activity whenever the imported `MAX_PRODUCT_ACTIVITIES` window is full. The definitions are now read: `peritus-app-protocol/src/product/interaction.rs:75-78` sets **256 entries** and **8,192 bytes per text/detail field**. Its constructors independently reject larger fields or collections at lines 139-141 and 192-196.
- Leading whitespace in a pending stream is discarded after 256 valid bytes at lines 174-176. Invalid UTF-8 is rejected explicitly rather than displayed. Persistence-failure presentation may evict another activity to insert its error at lines 253-302.
- Effect: the interaction view cannot expose complete indefinitely growing activity/text history through this window. This is a presentation/history boundary; an execution-duration restriction is not established by these reads. Durable retention and client pagination remain pending.

### L026 — Governance failures become persistent execution/admission barriers

- `product_run/interaction/live.rs:26-111` converts control-store/read errors into governing-context stop text, an empty reference-authority context, revision `u64::MAX`, protection of the entire workspace, and no host permissions. The error's original class is not retained by several of these fallback return values.
- Lines 153-207 explicitly reject provider requests and input incorporation after the shared `persistence_failed` flag is set. Tool admission at lines 247-276 yields when the supplied input generation differs from durable state. Goal admission at lines 373-380 stops on Paused or Inactive.
- `interaction.rs:235-251` uses `pending_record_input(record).unwrap_or(false)`, so an input-inspection error can become an absence of pending input. These are fail-closed authority/durability choices; their recovery and user-actionability need caller inspection before claiming a permanent lockup.

### L027 — Governed live execution disables semantic compaction

- `product_run/interaction/live.rs:150-152` unconditionally returns `false` from `allows_semantic_compaction` for this live conversation port.
- Potential daily-driving effect: a growing governed conversation cannot use this automatic semantic-compaction capability. `peritus-agent/src/developer/execution.rs:94-127` now verifies this disables the **legacy semantic-compaction path** only when no local context port is in use. With a local port, context assembly runs instead; `local_context/port.rs:194-202` separately performs local compaction/checkpoint work. Explicit compaction and local capacity/recovery implementations remain pending. This declaration alone does not prove that all forms of compaction are disabled.

### L028 — Accounting failures cancel the active run

- `product_run/execution/goal.rs:59-96` polls durable goal progress after an initial 100 ms and then at 1,000 ms intervals while accounting remains active. These are polling cadences, not elapsed execution deadlines.
- Any error from `observe_goal_clock` cancels both the run flag and provider cancellation and stops accounting. Lines 98-108 set `persistence_failed` and retain a goal-progress persistence error. A final observation failure records the error while returning the original execution result.
- Structural coupling: an accounting storage failure can stop otherwise progressing model/tool work, and the resulting shared failure flag blocks subsequent admission (L026). `product_control/goal.rs:158-200,292-335` confirms that each governed progress update loads the execution record, persists a host operation, and loads state again; storage errors propagate to this cancellation path. Its reservations admit ordinary execution with no goal at lines 28-30 and 99-101. Pure goal-transition budget enforcement remains pending. Whether SQLite's 250 ms contention deadline (L019) reaches this path requires those remaining reads.

### L029 — Application-protocol default and negotiated capacity ceilings

- `peritus-app-protocol/src/limits.rs:40-53,240-243` defaults to production codec limits (L009), **16 version ranges**, **64 feature names**, **4,096 retained idempotency entries**, **64 subscription topics**, **256 unacknowledged events**, **256 KiB artifact chunks**, **64 prompt choices**, **64 KiB terminal chunks**, **4 KiB diagnostic text**, and **256 remaining-work items**.
- Lines 97-118 negotiate the pointwise minimum of both peers' capacities. Constructor validation at lines 198-237 requires positive values that fit their chosen enclosing codec dimensions; these application dimensions are not individually hard-capped to production by this constructor.
- Effect depends on the owning state machine: chunk/page boundaries can permit unbounded total progress, while retained state and one-message collections can reject work. All declarations are recorded; actual owner/caller enforcement is pending rather than assumed identical across dimensions.

### L030 — Product task, detail, deliverable, and page admission

- `peritus-app-protocol/src/product.rs:38-43` declares **64 KiB task text**, **1 MiB per run detail field**, and **256 runs per page**. Task-construction callers remain pending; the daemon list caller was read in L015 and supports an offset.
- `ProductDeliverable::checked` at lines 67-78 rejects an empty changed-path collection, more than **65,535 changed paths or successful commands**, and fields above 1 MiB. Some restore constructors additionally require a successful command. Absolute/traversal/Git paths are rejected at lines 79-85 as authority/path constraints.
- Large deliverables can be rejected even when their underlying work succeeded. One-page size does not by itself imply old runs are deleted; retention/pagination client behavior remains pending.

### L031 — Legacy goal-tool replay is a schema barrier

- `peritus-daemon/src/product_control/goal/replay.rs:17-22` rejects a tool-goal reservation/completion when its current identity is absent but the legacy identity exists, returning `ControlError::UnsupportedSchema` instead of migrating/reconciling that legacy operation.
- `goal.rs:112-125,147-155` propagates this through live tool admission/completion. Scope is exact legacy identity, not every older conversation. Other migration/recovery paths have not yet been read.
- `goal.rs:356-363` maps Paused/Cancelled to Paused admission and WaitingForUser/Blocked/Achieved to Inactive; Active/Pausing remain accepted. These durable goal states stop work through L026. Budget triggers and resume paths remain pending.

### L032 — Goal text/count representation and checked counter exhaustion

- `peritus-product-runner/src/control/goal.rs:103,165-168` limits objective text to **8,192 bytes**, criterion descriptions to **2,048 bytes**, and transition reasons to **512 bytes** through ControlText. `goal/lifecycle.rs:17-25` and `goal/validation.rs:43-57` require a nonempty criteria collection of at most **65,535**, including a mandatory RunnerAcceptance criterion.
- `goal/accounting.rs:32-41,111-118` uses `u32` request/tool/retry/compaction/failover counters and `u64` token/time/resource counters. `goal/execution.rs:24,43-64,93,134-153,288-289` returns Capacity on checked arithmetic exhaustion; summary queries saturate across roles at `accounting.rs:129-135,159-165`. These are representation limits rather than smaller synthetic daily-work quotas.
- The complete goal implementation has now been read: it does **not** enforce the former request/tool/token/day ceilings. `goal/tests.rs:28-53` asserts continued admission beyond those former values; this audit has read those tests, not rerun them. Provider/storage/context ceilings remain independent.

### L033 — Optional run horizon and provider-circuit lifetime

- `peritus-product-runner/src/budget.rs:34-45,149-163` accepts an optional caller-selected elapsed horizon; `None` imposes none. A selected zero duration is rejected, and elapsed time strictly above the selected horizon returns ProductRunnerErrorKind::Budget at event/resource boundaries (lines 68-72,122-130).
- The daemon ordinary launch was already read with `max_elapsed: None` (L023). Other callers and configuration inputs remain pending; retaining a user-selected horizon is distinct from imposing an unrequested default.
- Lines 110-120 retain an unavailable-provider circuit in a per-run set until an explicit caller closes it. Whether retry reconnects/reopens the same native context depends on the pending failover/turn callers.
- Fallible host-resource probing at lines 122-135 also propagates as a run error even without an elapsed horizon. Actual probe exclusions, traversal bounds, and error behavior remain pending.

### L034 — Goal continuation requires lifecycle/evidence admission

- `goal/execution.rs:179-235` makes incomplete or stale acceptance evidence Blocked, missing external evidence WaitingForUser, and recovery-required settlement Blocked. `goal/lifecycle.rs:114-118` marks only Active as automatically restart-eligible.
- `lifecycle.rs:149-162` permits explicit resume from Paused, WaitingForUser, or Blocked while retaining history and usage. It rejects resume from Active, Pausing, Achieved, or Cancelled. Changes to a confirmed objective or previously achieved evidence can block continuation at lines 179-211.
- These are explicit goal/evidence/pause semantics, not elapsed quotas. Daily-driving concern is whether product callers classify transient infrastructure/capacity errors as a terminal lifecycle state and supply a usable recovery path; those callers remain partly pending (L026/L028).

### L035 — Tool writes and completed-command receipts impose a tighter file ceiling

- `peritus-product-runner/src/developer_tools/executor.rs:27` defines **2 MiB per file**. `executor/effects.rs:203-208,234-253` rejects larger direct writes and larger patched final files. `checkpoint_observer.rs:129-170` repeats those checks during preflight.
- `checkpoint_observer.rs:333-355` reads the completed command's changed scoped file and rejects its receipt above **2 MiB**, even after the command succeeded. This ceiling is tighter than the checkpoint's 8 MiB bound (L003) and independently blocks artifact-producing commands.
- Structural issue: workspace state, file-edit payload, checkpoint capture, and post-command effect evidence have different capacities. A command can pass preflight under one capacity and fail durable settlement under another. Its later recovery/settlement caller remains pending.

### L036 — Command preflight checkpoints every enrolled file

- `executor.rs:243-257` calls `prepare_effect_checkpoint` before dispatching the command. `executor/checkpoint_observer.rs:213-230` reads every current in-place scope path and invokes the pre-mutation observer for each, rejecting directory targets and scope changes.
- Combined with the daemon live hook (L003), a build/verification command is refused when an enrolled file cannot be checkpointed, even before its actual mutation set is known. `execution/checkpoint.rs:89-133` now verifies forwarding into the daemon live ConversationView; `turn.rs:280-291` installs this observer on writer/fixer tools. The full precommand chain is verified.
- Post-effect receipt recovery at lines 64-107 requires exact unchanged write/patch/delete results; reappearance or divergent contents require reconciliation. These effect-identity fences are recorded separately from the size limits.

### L037 — Selected horizons synthesize a completion reserve and clamp command execution

- `developer_tools/command_budget.rs:9,56-87,96-103` reserves **one fifth of the selected horizon**, at least one second for a whole-second horizon, at most **300 seconds**, and no more than the horizon. Remaining command time is floored to whole seconds after subtracting that reserve.
- It clamps a requested timeout, assigns the remaining allowance when the command has no requested timeout, and refuses to start when zero remains. `executor/command.rs:42-44,67-69,167-188` enforces this allowance. `None` horizon has no reserve and preserves the optional requested timeout.
- Explicit `timeout_seconds` must be positive and at most **u64::MAX / 1,000** for millisecond representation. Terminal dimensions are **1..65,535** at command start (defaults 24×80) and **0..65,535** at resize; downstream validation remains pending.
- Daily-driving status: ordinary daemon launch currently has no run horizon; other horizon callers are pending. This reserve is an additional policy deadline inside any selected horizon, and timeout recovery text discourages an equivalent longer retry at `command.rs:200-206`.

### L038 — Inspection-loop feedback has a finite observation window and does not enforce convergence

- `executor.rs:28-30` and `executor/effects.rs:120-159` issue feedback after **12 tools without delivery progress**, at most **two nudges** until a qualifying workspace mutation or successful declared external effect resets them. Read-only modes bypass this delivery-progress check.
- `executor/inspection_progress.rs:9-10,50-59,79-108` retains **16 distinct inspection fingerprints** and warns on the first identical repeat still visible to the model. It clears/reset state on qualifying mutation or new evidence; evidence no longer visible can be reread without a repeat warning.
- Effect: these numbers bound detection/feedback, not task execution. The code returns warnings and continues; it supplies no durable stage convergence rule. A changing or sufficiently wide inspection loop can evade exact-repeat feedback. Model-loop response and retained-stage behavior remain pending.

### L039 — Tool authority and mode gates can suppress process work

- `developer_tools/executor.rs:142-155,200-239` requires Read+Write+Process for command start/stdin/resize/signal, even if a particular requested command is observational. Owned command polling/recovery/cancel remain available after permission revocation.
- Read-only mode permits only list/search/read; it rejects every process/mutation tool before effect dispatch. Access policy and grounding add separate task-scope restrictions. These are explicit authority boundaries, not counted as artificial deadlines, but their effect on review/planning verification is recorded.
- Actual user permission defaults, mode selection, protected-path refresh, and usable recovery from revoked/failed control state remain pending.

### L040 — Build concurrency heuristic is enforced as an execution ceiling

- `developer_tools/resources.rs:10-11,23-33` estimates **2 GiB per build job** and clamps recommended parallelism to **1..8**, regardless of a larger usable host. It samples available CPU/cgroup and memory once when the tool executor is constructed.

- Lines 66-78 inject concurrency environment defaults across languages; **CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is separately capped at 2**. `executor/command.rs:158` calls authorization before any command starts and passes these bindings into the runtime.
- Daily-driving effect: a heuristic recommendation becomes a hard refusal even when the user/host could safely run more workers. Real OS/cgroup limits and the added fixed/heuristic policy are distinct. Runtime environment merge/override behavior remains pending.

### L041 — Workspace inspection truncates or omits evidence

- `developer_tools/inspection.rs:31-68` lists at default depth **3**, clamped to **1..12**, and stops after **2,000 entries** with `truncated=true`. The response provides no continuation cursor in this file; callers can target narrower paths. Child errors are skipped.
- Search at lines 99,127-150 returns default **200**, at most **1,000 matches**, silently skips files above **2 MiB**, unsupported/non-UTF-8 content and child I/O errors, and stops with `truncated=true` at its result ceiling.

Selected individual line accumulation above **2 MiB** fails at lines 220-224. Multiple line output can grow before a separate `effect::limit` truncates it; `effect.rs:9,49-54` now verifies the separate **512 KiB output-prefix cap plus a truncation marker**; read replies retain the requested line interval despite that cut.

Explicit pagination/narrowing can help, but this implementation does not establish full coverage from one successful observation.

- `peritus-agent/src/developer/retry.rs:18-20,129-157` supplies **250 ms base delay**, **30,000 ms maximum delay**, and deterministic jitter up to **250,000 millionths (25%)** to the retry planner. These wait parameters are backoff policy, not a total execution deadline.

### L051 — Same-provider recovery has a three-invocation cap without material progress

- `peritus-product-runner/src/failover.rs:12,26-35` permits fewer than **three failed same-provider role invocations** before recovery stops; the first two failures retry, the third does not. This is independent of each invocation's default three per-turn attempts (L050).

- `peritus-product-runner/src/execution/checkpoint.rs:244-257` attempts a before-checkpoint/content-hash/after-checkpoint identity capture **three times**, then returns a Repository error if concurrent workspace changes prevent a stable observation.

### L054 — Selected run horizons also impose a separate phase-finalization reserve

- `peritus-product-runner/src/execution/deadline.rs:7-8,21-22,25-57` reserves **one tenth of the selected horizon**, clamped between **one second and 60 seconds**, each capped by the horizon. It subtracts this from active time and refuses Design/Writer/Reviewer/Fixer phase admission when remaining time is at or below the reserve.

- `execution/conversation.rs:245-252` converts the durable `u64` conversation revision to `u32` when building its request prefix and rejects overflow. Thus revisions above **4,294,967,295** cannot enter this conversation path even though the governing port exposes `u64` revisions.

Do not generalize writer/fixer grounding barriers to every conversational answer; segment policy text still tells the model to re-ground (`conversation.rs:236-239`).

- `peritus-product-runner/src/local_context/storage.rs:178-190` retries the lineage owner file lock only while elapsed time is below **250 ms**, sleeping **5 ms** between attempts. It then returns “lineage already has an owner or cannot be locked,” without preserving the original lock error class.

### L067 — Referenced and quarantined artifacts keep consuming the logical quota

### L068 — Artifact writer has bounded temporary-name allocation and fatal write admission

- `writer.rs:149-173,181-235` requires expected bytes <= positive declared bytes <= configured maximum, rejects overflow or excess chunks, and makes the writer unusable after a write failure. Exact final size/digest is an integrity requirement distinct from the configurable byte cap.

A newly published object is removed for quota/arithmetic failure; other catalog errors are returned after publication. `recovery.rs:179-199` contains uncataloged published bytes by quarantining them, then removes them on a subsequent recovery pass; this does not repair the failed local-context publication automatically.

Missing recorded bytes abort recovery (`157,174,309-314`); noncanonical names, nonregular entries, or unexpected temporary-directory contents also abort it (`231-291`).
