The same wrapper is used for hypotheses, alternatives, prediction falsification and selection explanations.
- Consequence: Ordinary multiline rationale cannot be represented even when it is well within the byte limit. This is an input-format blocker for evolution evidence, not a model execution deadline or demonstrated installed-session failure.
- Repair direction: Define allowed whitespace explicitly and preserve ordinary structured prose. Restrict unsafe control sequences without making every explanation a single line. No tests run.

### L447 F0 accepts mandatory failure-class predictions that its attribution engine can never confirm

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/change/prediction.rs:160-170`, `src/attribution/engine.rs:68-69`, `src/attribution/record.rs:158-160`, `src/selection/engine.rs:85-90` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Prediction construction admits a FailureClass subject for metrics other than TaskPassAtK. Attribution unconditionally returns Unavailable with UnsupportedFailureClass for that subject. Every mandatory prediction whose result is not Confirmed counts as a mandatory failure, and selection requires that count to be zero.
- Consequence: A syntactically accepted mandatory failure-class prediction makes its candidate permanently ineligible through the current engine. More runs or waiting cannot satisfy it. The mandatory-evidence rule itself is a valid quality contract; admitting a requirement the engine cannot evaluate is the blocker. No installed campaign was reproduced.
- Repair direction: Validate evaluability at admission or implement class-specific measurements and uncertainty handling. Return a repairable unsupported-capability result before freezing a campaign requirement. No tests run.

### L448 F0 promotion always requires resource measurements, even with unconstrained thresholds and unrelated objectives

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/selection/engine.rs:39-46,52-153`, `src/binding/policy.rs:53-111`, `src/selection/tests.rs`, `src/qualification/evidence.rs:189-208` in the same crate.

Choosing other ranking objectives or setting a ceiling to u64::MAX does not disable that availability prerequisite. Trace/teardown requirements have explicit optional flags; resource measurements do not. The qualification fixture supplies every metric.
- Consequence: An evaluation with legitimately unavailable provider cost or token measurements cannot promote a candidate through F0, even when the caller intended no constraint on that metric. Additional correctness evidence does not remove the unavailable criterion. These are frozen quality-policy prerequisites, not elapsed-time enforcement; the blocker is lack of a representable optional requirement and capability validation. This audit did not run a provider evaluation.
- Repair direction: Distinguish required measurements, optional measurements and ranking objectives in the policy. Validate required measurement capability before admitting a campaign; preserve unavailable values honestly rather than inventing passing observations. No tests run.

### L449 F0 publication is permanently bounded to sixteen delivery claims

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/durability/directive.rs:17,206-258`; C0 exhaustion semantics documented in L251/L265.
- Behavior: Both CampaignDecision and HarnessActivation directives are built with MAX_ATTEMPTS=16. This limit counts C0 delivery claims and has no F0 configuration, unlimited representation or replenishment command. It is separate from campaign evaluation attempts and human approval.
- Consequence: Sufficient delivery failures can exhaust durable publication even though the intended artifact and activation remain valid and recoverable. RetryPublication alone does not provide a fresh eligible claim once C0 has exhausted the row. This is an explicit synthetic retry ceiling, not a finding that sixteen failures occurred in the live session.
- Repair direction: Keep durable publication intent pending until confirmed completion, explicit cancellation or an actionable integrity failure. Bound pacing and concurrent work independently of lifetime recoverable deliveries, and provide authorized reconciliation without changing evidence identity. No tests run.

### L450 Ordinary F0 committed-command replay fails after later checkpoint progress

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/durability/campaign.rs:192-228`, `src/durability/pointer.rs:165-201` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The journal resolves an exact committed command before current-head validation, but F0 then loads the current checkpoint and requires it to equal that command's original successor state and sequence. After any later transition, replaying the identical old command returns a quarantining recovery error despite an exact durable command/event receipt.
- Consequence: A delayed retry or receipt lookup can be classified as corruption solely because useful work has advanced. Immediate replay before another transition is accepted. This finding concerns ordinary campaign/pointer commits; atomic activation has a separate approve-once resolution contract and is not assumed identical.
- Repair direction: Validate the immutable producing transaction and its original installed state independently of the latest projection. Return the existing receipt without regressing current state, retaining conflicting-request and causal-fence rejection for genuinely new mutations. No tests run.

### L451 F0 recovery can report terminal completion without checking retained artifact/evidence observations

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/runtime/recovery.rs:11-19,48-68`, `src/durability/directive.rs:224-247`, `src/runtime/publication.rs:46-85` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Recovery checks artifact_verified and evidence_admitted only when publication_directive is true. With an Active pointer and terminal campaign, false publication_directive yields Complete even when both owner observations are false. Promotion/rollback activation creates a separate publication directive; publication ACK occurs after evidence admission, but ACK status alone is not a check that the owners still retain matching content.
- Consequence: The F0 classifier alone cannot distinguish a fully published terminal activation from one with acknowledged/absent pending delivery but missing referenced owner records. A pending directive still produces the appropriate reconciliation decision. Higher-level integrity scans may catch owner loss; this is a recovery-contract gap, not proof that the current daemon ignored corruption or deleted context.
- Repair direction: Derive required publication obligations from durable activation/evidence state and verify their owner receipts before declaring completion. Treat delivery state as transport progress rather than the complete publication truth. No tests run.

### L452 F0's accepted bounds disagree with its attribution and assessment persistence schema

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/limits.rs:22-33,63-94`, `src/attribution/record.rs:124-135`, `src/wire/semantic/attribution.rs:22-29`, `src/selection/engine.rs:52-153`, `src/campaign/reducer/transition.rs:160-183`, `src/wire/semantic/selection.rs:42-45`, `src/wire/semantic/state/campaign.rs:95-98` in that crate; codec collection ceiling documented in L009.
- Behavior: Attribution permits 65,536 entries, but its single canonical collection uses the codec's 65,535 maximum. EvolutionLimits also accepts criteria=1 through 13. Assessment always produces fourteen results and campaign admission does not compare that count with the frozen criteria limit. Complete-state decoding does require all fourteen and a limit of at least fourteen.
- Consequence: The advertised maximum attribution cannot be serialized. A campaign with a small accepted criteria limit can admit and encode an assessment that its own checkpoint decoder rejects during recovery. These are source-derived boundary cases; no fixture was constructed or executed in this audit.
- Repair direction: Make admission, serialization and restore share one representability contract. Remove meaningless tunable criteria counts for a fixed schema, and page attribution independently of workload size rather than exposing incompatible maxima. No tests run.

### L453 An accepted out-of-range probability threshold cannot survive F0 wire decoding

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/change/prediction.rs:85-118,151-176`, `src/wire/semantic/change.rs:251-285`, `src/wire/campaign.rs:32-44,350-363` in the same crate.
- Behavior: MetricValue exposes ProbabilityMillionths directly. Its probability helper rejects values above 1,000,000, but Prediction::new only checks numeric variant compatibility and subject/metric rules, so direct enum construction bypasses the range check. Semantic writing emits the raw u32, while semantic reading always calls the bounded helper.
- Consequence: An accepted prediction can encode successfully and then fail canonical read/replay. For example, a directly constructed ProbabilityMillionths(1,000,001) threshold is incompatible with the wire contract despite passing the prediction constructor. This is an admission/restore mismatch, not a legitimate deadline; the probability range itself is mathematically required. No executed reproduction is claimed.
- Repair direction: Enforce numeric domain invariants at every public admission boundary or use a validated probability type that cannot be bypassed. Verify encode/decode parity before committing accepted semantic state. No tests run.

### L454 F0 wraps complete growing checkpoints in a fixed eight-MiB opaque payload

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/wire/campaign.rs:279-281,318-330`, `src/wire/pointer.rs:299-301,338-350`, `src/wire/semantic/campaign.rs:9-10,75-77`, `src/wire/semantic/state/campaign.rs:13-62`, `src/wire/semantic/state/pointer.rs:14-42`, `src/durability/campaign.rs:34-48`, `src/durability/pointer.rs:33-47` in the same crate; production codec limits in L009.
- Behavior: Inner semantic codecs hard-code CodecLimits::PRODUCTION. Checkpoints serialize all retained manifests, diagnoses, evaluation metrics, attributions, assessments or pointer history into one byte vector; the outer frame writes that vector as a single bytes field. Its eight-MiB opaque-field limit applies even though the whole-message ceiling is sixteen MiB. F0 has no independent state-size configuration or incremental checkpoint representation.
- Consequence: Individually valid additions within every F0 collection/text bound can still make the next complete checkpoint uncommittable. Cancel/fail also serializes retained state, so it does not provide a general size-reduction path. Expanding an outer caller codec cannot lift the hard-coded inner contract. This is a source-derived scaling ceiling, not evidence that an evolution checkpoint reached it in the live run.
- Repair direction: Persist immutable evidence once by verified reference and checkpoint a paged projection. Reserve reliable control/settlement operations independently of aggregate evidence volume while preserving exact provenance and replay integrity. No tests run.

### L455 F0 repeats whole-state and whole-store work synchronously during attribution, commit and recovery

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/attribution/engine.rs:123-142`, `src/campaign/reducer/transition.rs:61-63`, `src/campaign/state.rs:260-288`, `src/durability/replay.rs:79-116,127-161`, `src/wire/campaign.rs:170-199,279-281,318-321`, `src/wire/pointer.rs:178-213,299-301,338-341`, `src/runtime/publication.rs:53-83` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Each task prediction performs an existence scan and another task/k scan through the complete pass-at-k vector. Transitions clone all nested prior campaign evidence and rebuild the collection digest. Commit prevalidates state encoding, clones it into a frame and encodes it again. Recovery loads all events, applies each reducer during frame checking and again in the replay loop, then decodes and compares the complete checkpoint. Every publication obtains a global journal integrity export and scans its artifact references before admitting evidence. These synchronous functions offer no cancellation/progress cursor.
- Consequence: Task attribution can cost O(predictions times task/k observations), and campaign replay repeatedly copies growing embedded evidence. Pointer history bounds cap its hot state but do not make the event journal finite. These are source-derived latency and memory-pressure risks; no benchmark, active-session stall or wall timeout is attributed to F0 here.
- Repair direction: Index task/k observations, reference immutable evidence, perform each checked reduction once and verify paged snapshots with authenticated replay cursors. Preserve integrity while providing resumable bounded work and observable progress. No tests run.

### L457 C5 request controls and identifier/media fields have additional fixed acceptance ceilings

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/request/options.rs:123-143`, `src/request/validation.rs:35-67`, `src/identity/public.rs`, `src/identity/sensitive.rs`, `src/content.rs:80-98,168-183`, `src/redaction.rs:28-40` in that crate; aggregate protocol maxima in L017.
- Behavior: Generation requires positive max_output_tokens and at most 64 stop strings. Each request allows at most 128 option extensions. Provider/tool/extension/output names and idempotency keys are capped at 128 bytes, model and request/response/item/tool-call/event identities at 512, cache identities at 1,024, MIME values at 128 and media references at 8,192. These constants have no widening/unlimited option. Negotiation separately takes the minimum of five positive profile/caller numeric ceilings; request output must fit the negotiated ceiling even for a profile declaring output enforcement Advisory.
- Consequence: Representable provider identifiers or request controls beyond these local constants are rejected before transport. The caps are schema/input acceptance limits, not session duration or cache TTL. Model capacity metadata and API-required generation controls must be distinguished from artificial execution cutoffs; no installed request hitting these exact bounds was observed here.
- Repair direction: Ground field constraints in versioned provider contracts, keep diagnostics bounded separately, and support evolving or paged representations where the provider actually accepts more. Keep advisory output requests distinct from guaranteed enforcement. No tests run.

### L458 C5 JSON has non-widenable depth/member ceilings checked after full parsing

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/schema.rs:23-72,95-110,210-245,272-289,292-329`, `src/json_duplicates.rs:5-8,32-49,62-76` in the same crate.

Byte and string ceilings derive from ProtocolLimits. Parsing first constructs the complete serde JSON tree, then recursively scans the source again to detect duplicate keys, then checks domain depth/member/string limits and produces another canonical byte buffer. Object canonicalization collects/sorts all keys. Schemas reject nonlocal references.
- Consequence: Valid larger local structures cannot be represented even within the provider's capacity. A tight member/depth setting does not bound initial parse/allocation to that selected setting; total input bytes and library parser behavior still constrain the work. This is a source-derived resource/acceptance limit, not a wall timeout or measured stall. Duplicate rejection and preventing ambient remote-reference fetches are integrity/authority requirements.
- Repair direction: Validate chosen structural bounds during parsing, preserve duplicate rejection, and separate provider/schema representability from bounded working memory. Support references or paging without introducing ambient file/network authority. No tests run.

### L459 C5's complete request constructor admits unsatisfiable tool selection and unsupported semantic continuation

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/tool.rs:51-62`, `src/request/model.rs:38-73`, `src/request/validation.rs:11-32,70-146`, `src/request/options.rs:70-104`, `src/capability/profile.rs:160-169` in the same crate.

Continuation without a sequence is semantic; validation requires ResumableResponse only for exact cursors and never checks the profile's ResumeKind for semantic continuation. Required capability negotiation does not fill these cross-field gaps.

Actual transport may reject or omit such options; adapter behavior remains individually audited. This is a source-derived admission trap, not permission to fabricate continuation support or bypass tool authority.

### L460 C5 canonical request identity has a separate mandatory 512-MiB total ceiling

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/canonical.rs:19-41,58-100`, `src/request/model.rs:165-187,197-205` in the same crate.
- Behavior: canonical_bytes always uses a 512-MiB ceiling. canonical_bytes_bounded permits only positive smaller values. Its writer also independently caps collections at 1,100,000, strings at 32 MiB, bytes fields at 256 MiB and depth at 128. Fingerprinting and semantic idempotency encode the complete ordered conversation/tool/options request again rather than using a persisted streaming digest.
- Consequence: Per-field-valid retained conversation can eventually become unrepresentable as one canonical request; increasing caller storage above 512 MiB is rejected. Smaller chosen ceilings are enforced incrementally before appending each field, so this path does not simply build all bytes then truncate them. Full repeated encoding remains synchronous work proportional to request size. No live request of this size was reproduced.

### L461 C5 nested admission and persistence checks can disagree under selected limits

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/request/validation.rs:35-67,77-101`, `src/canonical_decode/primitive.rs:57-90`, `src/canonical_decode/content.rs:132-138`, `src/event_codec/encode.rs:19-36,119-128`, `src/event_codec/decode.rs:159-164,206-218,290-302`, `src/message_codec.rs:17-31,39-57` in the same crate.

Canonical reconstruction does recheck these nested constructors. Event encoding uses a shared maximum across domains, whereas fragment decoding specifically applies max_event_bytes. For example, a two-byte fragment constructed under production limits can encode under a selected one-byte event limit when the other codec byte maxima permit two bytes, then fail decoding under that same selected profile. Message-archive encoding likewise trusts nested values.

The dedicated extension-byte maximum is not consistently applied to ProviderExtension: request/event extension decoding uses JsonBounds::value, while reasoning replay explicitly uses max_extension_bytes. This is a source-derived API mismatch, not a reproduced installed-session failure. Existing inspected round-trip fixtures construct small nested values under the same production limits.

Reject incompatible selected limits before publication, and distinguish extension payload policy from tool JSON policy. No tests run.

### L462 C5 archives, events and rate observations add compiled ceilings beyond request bounds

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/message_codec.rs:6-7,17-31,60-72`, `src/event_codec/primitive.rs:5-19`, `src/rate_limit.rs:90-104`, `src/event_codec/decode.rs:220-228` in the same crate.

Event envelopes have another fixed 64-MiB total ceiling, collection maximum 1,024 and depth maximum 32. String and byte bounds combine several domain maxima. A rate-limit observation must contain between one and 64 windows; it cannot carry more provider dimensions even if the encoded frame would fit.
- Consequence: a conversation valid for the 512-MiB canonical-request encoder can exceed the separate 64-MiB archive format. These APIs expose no larger-frame or paged representation. Provider reset values, retry-after values and cache TTLs are inert observations here; they do not expire local sessions or impose a wall-clock timeout. The archive ceiling's installed effect depends on its separately tracked callers.

### L463 C5 reconstruction materializes full bounded content before aggregate request checks

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/canonical_decode.rs:35-67`, `src/canonical_decode/content.rs:11-53`, `src/request/validation.rs:44-55`, `src/message_codec.rs:46-55`, `src/event_codec/decode.rs:64-73` in the same crate.

Per-message counts and individual payloads are bounded, but aggregate request limits are enforced after their allocation. Canonical request, message and event decoders then encode the reconstructed value again for byte parity, retaining the original input while producing a complete second byte buffer. These are synchronous operations with no progress cursor or cancellation parameter.

Fixed frame and nested limits still bound the formats; this is not an unbounded-parser claim or a measured explanation of the current lockup. No benchmark run.

### L464 C5 retry algebra still requires a finite attempt and delay policy

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/retry.rs:72-94,119-128,170-178,192-205`, `tests/retry_matrix.rs:32-44,92-120` in the same crate; layered production policies are separately documented in L228.
- Behavior: max_attempts is a mandatory positive u32 with no Unlimited form. Attempts stop before scheduling when attempt plus one reaches that value. max_elapsed_millis is optional and None genuinely disables this planner's elapsed horizon. Base delay must be positive, max_delay must be at least base, and a provider Retry-After above max_delay produces a terminal planning refusal even with no elapsed horizon. The pure planner itself neither sleeps nor kills a request.
- Consequence: removing wall-clock limits alone leaves count and provider-delay blockers in the recovery contract. The ten-second elapsed horizon, four attempts and two-second delay in retry_matrix are fixture inputs, not installed defaults. Ambiguous acceptance and partial output without exact resumption are independent integrity constraints, not synthetic deadlines.
- Repair direction: separate ongoing, user-cancellable recovery scheduling from finite request budgets, and retain exact identity/acceptance facts while waiting the provider's required delay. Provide an explicit unbounded attempt policy rather than a sentinel numeric maximum. No tests run.

### L465 C5 exponential retry backoff can wrap to zero despite a positive minimum

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/retry.rs:192-197,208-217`.
- Behavior: the exponential delay uses checked_shl with a shift already clamped to 63. checked_shl rejects an out-of-range shift count, but does not detect discarded high bits. Thus its unwrap_or(u64::MAX) does not protect arithmetic overflow in these allowed shifts. With base_delay_millis 100, attempt 63 or greater, no Retry-After and zero jitter, the shifted value is zero and the calculated delay is zero despite validation requiring a positive base.
- Consequence: a caller permitting enough safe retries can lose all backoff and repeatedly resubmit immediately. This is a reachable source-level planner defect; currently audited production layers with smaller retry counts do not establish that the live session reached this case. Removing those count limits without fixing the arithmetic would expose it more broadly.
- Repair direction: calculate exponential growth with saturating multiplication or an explicit overflow predicate, then apply the intended delay policy. Preserve nonzero scheduled waits and cancellation across long recovery sequences. No tests run.

### L470 Compatible API defaults retain finite retry and private production capacities

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/config.rs:21-22,159-172,189-204,242-262,315-331`, `src/client.rs:142-180,211-228,280-283` in the same crate.

### L471 Compatible profiles exclude all provider-side continuation and several unused capabilities

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/profile.rs:224-257,260-271`, `src/request/validation.rs:15-45`, `src/request.rs:29-37`, `src/request/responses.rs:21-24` in the same crate.

Any Unknown capability anywhere in the profile is rejected, as is any supported capability without a mapped implementation even if the current request does not use it. Requests reject every continuation, storage/background setting, cache setting, reasoning control, audio/document and unresolved media. Only Draft202012 schemas are accepted; a parallel-call count narrower than the negotiated count is rejected because the wire maps a boolean only. Responses additionally rejects seed/stops.

Persistent local conversation replay is still possible; stateless provider invocation alone does not mean that the local session is ephemeral. Availability depends on the exact adapter contract, and removing these checks alone cannot invent provider resume guarantees. Whole-profile unknown rejection can prevent a supported basic request until its profile is normalized.

Add reviewed provider-side resume implementations where available, and retain explicit unsupported recovery rather than silently replacing the context. No tests run.

### L472 Compatible Retry-After parsing silently loses provider scheduling information

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/client/metadata.rs:66,72-82,166-172,183-196`, `src/client.rs:211-228`, `src/config.rs:196-200` in the same crate.

Larger integers or any other representation, including an HTTP-date, become None rather than a retained unsupported scheduling observation. A retained delay above the default two-second policy causes RetryPolicy::plan to return an error before the already-built normalized HTTP failure can be emitted.
- Consequence: one response can cause an immediate default backoff after its provider-required wait was discarded; another can become generic InvalidRetry instead of preserving RateLimited/status/acceptance facts. ### L476 Compatible wire and terminal formats narrow otherwise accepted content capacities

### L477 Compatible normalization expands IDs and packs indices beyond the original value contract

### L478 Hosted reasoning accumulation repeatedly scans and serializes all retained reasoning

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/hosted_reasoning.rs:28-87`, `src/stream/chat.rs:246-253`, `src/stream/chat/hosted.rs:125-155`, `src/stream/responses_state.rs:103-121` in the same crate.

### L479 Compatible streams can hide a known malformed suffix behind an already queued completion

A later data frame in that same parsed batch is rejected because terminal is already set, but the failure is appended after the queued completion. The owned stream returns the completion and permanently stops pulling at its first terminal event. A later network chunk is not read once the adapter is terminal either.

Tool arguments remain buffered until finalized, structured text is withheld until whole-value completion, and finalized text/arguments must exactly match retained deltas. - Consequence: legal-width source identities can overflow after local suffixing; flattening can collide; missing sequence events may be detected only through downstream state failure. General output bounds do not remove the narrower whole-value/fragment/argument limits, synchronous copies/parsing, or growing history scans already recorded for healing. No provider claim that zero/gaps are valid is inferred here.
- Repair direction: define explicit provider sequence semantics, preserve collision-free tuple coordinates and bounded identifier derivation, publish meaningful buffered progress, and make assembly limits compatible with the normalized protocol and durable resume state. No tests run.

### L502 MCP finite admission and response backpressure can block cancellation notifications

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-mcp/src/server.rs:31-62,130-143,189-263,268-281,549-560`; `src/bridge.rs:225-269` in the same crate.
- Behavior: production limits are 2 MiB per message, 32 in-flight requests, and 128 entries per page; limits must be positive. Saturated admission immediately returns an internal error instead of queuing work. Responses share a bounded queue of the same request count. The input loop awaits sends of initialization, parse, duplicate-id, and overload responses. A slow writer/full response queue stops this loop from reading cancellation notifications. List bridge methods have no cancellation argument; other operations rely entirely on bridge cooperation without a cancellation select.

Increasing counts or adding a timeout does not repair the control-plane dependency. Positive-only validation also fails to check the semaphore's representable maximum before constructing it.
- Repair direction: give control notifications independent progress under response backpressure, define cancellation for every admitted method, and make admission/rejection recoverable with validated resource bounds. No installed MCP-server incident or test execution is claimed.

### L503 MCP task completion and disconnect handling lack active-session reconciliation

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-mcp/src/server.rs:130-177,180-265`.
- Behavior: request tasks are added to a JoinSet and joined only after the input loop ends; completed tasks accumulate throughout a long-lived connection. Clean EOF does not signal cancellation or abort active requests before waiting for every task. Writer failures are not selected alongside the input loop. A panicked request skips active-map removal, while task errors/panics are observed only after EOF. The server context/lifecycle is process-local and initialization is permitted exactly once.
- Consequence: a disconnected client can leave shutdown waiting indefinitely on bridge work, an idle reader can delay detection of a failed writer, and a panicked request can leave its identifier permanently classified active on the surviving connection. Long-lived sessions retain completed-task bookkeeping. These are ownership/reconciliation gaps; the absence of an arbitrary deadline is not itself the defect.
- Repair direction: reap completions while serving, react to writer/disconnect events, clean active identifiers through owned guards, and reconcile admitted work with durable daemon session authority before closing or reconnecting. No tests run.

A whole bridge result is converted/serialized before response-size rejection, which fails the writer rather than returning a per-request bounded result. Public resource/prompt projection DTOs described as bounded do not enforce per-field bounds. List pagination first obtains the entire bridge collection, then slices it using an unversioned numeric offset into the current collection.

Count pagination does not bound page bytes or avoid full collection allocation, and concurrent collection changes can skip/repeat entries. These format/version/resource boundaries are distinct from local deadlines.

Invocation context additionally requires a numeric deadline_millis; there is no deadline-free wire representation. The manifest schema and current protocol support are version one.

Removing a Tokio timeout at a caller alone cannot eliminate the compulsory SDK deadline/lifetime semantics. ### L507 Plugin payload and frame constructors disagree with fixed deserialization limits

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-sdk/src/payload.rs:21-65,89-105,108-159`; `src/canonical.rs:8-78`; `src/framing.rs:15-54`; `src/protocol/wire.rs:5-58`; `src/protocol/request_wire.rs:41-74`; `src/protocol/response_wire.rs:96-134` in the same crate.

Payload validation/canonical rendering traverses complete Value trees; protocol serialization converts nested payloads into fresh Value trees and frame encoding allocates the whole JSON before enforcing its positive u32 frame maximum. Duplicate JSON members are already collapsed by Value parsing, so canonicalization cannot establish their original uniqueness.

Legitimate decimal-valued tool inputs/results fail this plugin representation. Whole-value conversion/canonicalization and escaping can produce a late frame-bound failure after earlier logical admission; widening frame bytes does not widen payload admission.

### L509 Plugin host lifetime quota can be exhausted by rejected work

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/quota.rs:16-55`; `src/host.rs:153-175,230-266,407-421`; `src/authority.rs:106-133`; `src/transport.rs:145-162` in the same crate.

Successful completion releases only active capacity; lifetime count never refills within an instance. Exhaustion is labelled RetryLater although waiting cannot restore it. Mandatory manifest/host invocation duration drives a Tokio response-read timeout. The authority grant must carry a nonzero deadline and is forwarded to the plugin, but the host neither checks it against a clock nor uses it to narrow the invocation timeout. Host configuration/narrowed quotas are not validated on construction/start.

A compulsory local duration survives the product's earlier deadline removals, while the separate purported authority deadline is not enforced consistently. No numeric production host defaults are inferred from the five-second/16-request test fixture.

### L510 Plugin cancellation and deadline handling can hang before termination

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/transport.rs:91-162,165-219`; `src/host.rs:230-266,314-332` in the same crate.
- Behavior: exchange first awaits a single transaction mutex, writes/flushed the complete request, and only then starts the cancellable response-read timeout. Queue wait and input writes have no cancellation select. On cancellation/timeout it awaits another full cancellation-frame write before termination. If the plugin has stopped reading stdin or the pipe is full, that write can wait indefinitely. Stop uses the same transaction and write path, so its shutdown timeout does not cover acquiring the transaction or sending shutdown.
- Consequence: local cancellation can be blocked by a different invocation, large input, or the attempt to deliver cancellation itself. Nominal invocation/startup/shutdown deadlines cover only response reads and cannot guarantee cleanup. Removing synthetic deadlines must be paired with interruptible ownership/control progress, not a blind deletion of the only eventual response exit.
- Repair direction: make queue/write/read ownership cancellation-aware, reserve a control path that cannot depend on the stalled plugin consuming stdin, and proceed with explicit termination/reconciliation when cooperative notification cannot progress. No tests run or hang reproduction claimed.

### L511 Plugin failed-state handling and queued authority cannot support durable recovery

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/host.rs:126-135,210-273,290-305,314-357`; `src/transport.rs:58-64,97-142,165-169`; `src/quota.rs:21-32` in the same crate.
- Behavior: all exchanges serialize through one transaction mutex despite higher concurrent-request quotas. Invocation lifecycle/authority/quota checks happen before queueing and are not rechecked after acquiring that mutex. Any exchange error, including a pre-cancelled token or request-encoding error before submission, marks the whole instance Failed; those paths need not terminate its process. Failed instances remain in the map and block start until stop removes them. Some invalid invocation status responses instead return RestartPlugin while leaving the lifecycle Ready. Registry, counters, transport handles, and lifecycle state have no persistence/reattachment API; process drop kills the child. Kill/wait errors are discarded.
- Consequence: cancellation of unsent work can disable the entire plugin, queued work can proceed using stale lifecycle/authority observations, and requested restart is not a direct available transition. Losing the host loses the process/context and evidence needed to distinguish completed effects. Higher admission concurrency does not create parallel wire progress.
- Repair direction: bind dispatch to fresh authority after admission, distinguish unsent cancellation from failed/possibly accepted execution, align recovery disposition with actual transitions, and journal invocation/instance identity with explicit reconnect or reconciliation semantics. No tests run.

The host keeps an immutable discovery snapshot. Start trust checks stored discovery digests rather than re-reading the artifact bytes before launch.

### L514 Telemetry queues impose finite item counts and bounded shutdown flushing

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/buffer/mod.rs:17-55`, `src/buffer/state.rs:105-186`, `src/export/pump.rs:83-139`, `src/export/types.rs`.

Enqueue constructs the encoded prefix before rejecting a new record. Capacity counts records, not their encoded bytes. Shutdown attempts at most the caller-selected batch count and returns Pending with queued records retained when that count is exhausted. Export and exporter shutdown are synchronous calls without a cancellation channel.
- Consequence: These controls can discard or reject observational records and can stall an exporter caller indefinitely. A large record still has large memory cost inside a small item-count queue. This crate's documented observational role does not establish that these controls themselves cancel agent work; that requires caller evidence. No telemetry session TTL is introduced here.

Synchronous exporters need an ownership and cancellation contract rather than an assumed timer guarantee. No tests run.

### L515 Failed telemetry export batches are rebuilt rather than pinned for retry

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/export/pump.rs:83-109`, `src/buffer/state.rs:105-186`, `src/export/types.rs`, `tests/buffering_export.rs:42-63`.
- Behavior: A pump reads a fresh prefix of the current queue for every flush. It does not retain the exact previously failed batch. Enqueue after a failure can extend a partially full batch; DropOldest can evict records in the failed batch. Batch identity includes record sequence/content, so these changes produce a different batch identity. Exact acknowledgements are checked before retirement, which is a necessary integrity guard.
- Consequence: The stated exact-batch retry behavior is not preserved across intervening enqueue. If remote acceptance happened before acknowledgement loss, rebuilding a different batch cannot by itself establish idempotent batch retry. Event-level downstream deduplication may compensate, but is not proved here. The test retries a full two-record batch without interleaved enqueue.
- Repair direction: Persist a pending export batch and its acknowledgement identity until resolved, and define how overflow interacts with records already in flight. Test acknowledgement loss plus interleaved enqueue and overflow. No tests run.

### L516 Telemetry projection and checkpoint recovery replay whole trace histories

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/projection.rs:148-233`, `src/recovery.rs:42-98`, `src/metrics.rs:155-172`.
- Behavior: Projection collects and globally sorts observations, then scans each trace's observations again for each ended span and clones associated diagnostics into that span. Diagnostics also remain standalone records. Recovery takes a complete projection, re-encodes and hashes the prefix from genesis to verify the checkpoint, then enqueues the entire suffix under the queue's current overflow policy.
- Consequence: Work grows with spans multiplied by observations plus sorting and copying; this is source-derived complexity, not a measured live stall. Recovery has no incremental cursor or cooperative cancellation in this layer. A smaller queue can reject or drop historical telemetry during recovery, with explicit counts. Checked metric counters are observational accounting, not agent execution quotas.
- Repair direction: Use durable verified projection cursors and per-span indexes, and preserve replay progress across capacity pressure. Define recovery loss separately from execution recovery. No tests run.

### L517 The newest telemetry checkpoint can block recovery despite retained older checkpoints

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/storage.rs:20-21`, `src/storage.rs:105-109`, `src/storage.rs:151-224`, `src/storage.rs:318-362`, `tests/checkpoint_recovery.rs:171-189`.
- Behavior: The store selects the highest checkpoint filename sequence and decodes only that file. A corrupt or incorrectly bound newest file fails loading without trying a retained older checkpoint. V1 checkpoints are rejected; V2 is an exact 152-byte format. Retention must be positive. Opening the store cleans matching temporary files under a single-owner assumption. Persisted identical checkpoints can retry finalization; mismatched content at the same sequence is rejected.

Format, binding and checksum checks are integrity requirements; removing those checks would not repair recoverability. Windows directory syncing is a no-op in this implementation, so the Unix durability path cannot certify Windows power-loss behavior.
- Repair direction: Preserve quarantine diagnostics for a bad newest checkpoint while selecting an older verified checkpoint and replaying the journal suffix. Make format migration and ownership explicit. No tests run.

The closed vocabulary currently has only 16 attribute keys and seven sensitivity classes, so those uniqueness rules are tighter in practice. SensitivePayload accepts only nonempty values of at most 16 MiB, even when the next operation merely omits their content. Decode allocates and reads collections under the general production codec bound before the smaller observation bounds are checked.

### L520 Trace recording treats wall-clock regression as an invalid lifecycle transition

A monotonic counter reset across restart also needs an explicit generation/continuation contract; retaining a span alone does not establish that contract. This is a source-derived rejection path, not a diagnosis of the installed session. The previously documented caller paths that propagate trace errors make such recording failures relevant to daily use.

Record clock discontinuities without turning them into execution authority. Test backward wall correction with forward causal progress and restart with a new monotonic origin. No tests run.

### L521 Every new durable trace observation replays the complete aggregate history

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-trace/src/storage.rs:102-119`, `src/projection/state.rs:263-295`, `src/projection/encoding.rs:10-71`, `src/recovery.rs:28-66`.

Applying each observation clones the current complete span map for failure atomicity. Observations retain both the decoded domain value and canonical frame bytes; event identities and spans are not retired. Projection encoding and invariant hashing copy the entire accumulated projection. Single-trace recovery loads the complete chain; all-trace recovery integrity-exports the entire journal.

There is no incremental projection cursor, chunked recovery, cancellation or progress callback in these paths. This is complexity derived from the code, not measured latency. Keeping sessions persistent will expose growing history rather than eliminating this cost.

Exact committed-command replay already resolves before history replay and should remain idempotent. No tests run.

### L522 Trace causal contracts require the exact latest event and classify missing predecessors as terminal integrity

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-trace/src/projection/fold.rs:23-39`, `src/projection/fold.rs:63-79`, `src/projection/state.rs:255-307`, `src/projection/mod.rs:60-74`, `src/error.rs:197-212`.

All declared predecessors must already exist in the same trace; trace session identity cannot change. A missing or superseded parent predecessor is CausalIntegrity, whose recovery class is TerminalIntegrity. Projection folding maps every trace failure to journal repair guidance.

There is no trace-local reobserve/replan distinction for that case. Exact ordering, duplicate-content binding and session association are necessary correctness contracts; they do not require treating every stale caller plan as corrupt authoritative history.
- Repair direction: Separate stale-plan rejection before commit from invalid committed history during replay, with actionable reobservation for the former. Preserve immutable committed identity and exact duplicate resolution. No tests run.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/status.rs:14-16`, `src/status.rs:262-319`, `src/status/porcelain.rs:15-55`, `src/status/porcelain.rs:261-277`.

### L529 Candidate creation and restoration scan every directory under a fixed entry limit

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/snapshot/support.rs:16`, `src/snapshot/support.rs:169-213`, `src/snapshot/operations.rs:28-52`, `src/snapshot/operations.rs:181-224`.
- Behavior: Before staging a candidate or restoring a snapshot, a synchronous recursive filesystem scan counts every entry, rejecting the 200,001st. It skips descent into the root .git metadata, but does not honor Git ignore rules for other directories. Any nested entry named .git is unsupported, including initialized submodules or nested worktrees. The scan has no resumable cursor, progress or cancellation hook.
- Consequence: Ignored dependency/build trees can block snapshots and rollback even when their files would not be staged. An initialized submodule is observable through status but its nested .git file blocks candidate creation/restoration. These are fixed compatibility and count barriers, not elapsed deadlines. Restoration subsequently uses read-tree followed by clean -fdx, so its effect contract also includes removing ignored/untracked content from that exact managed worktree.
- Repair direction: Define candidate content and protected nested repository handling explicitly, and preserve progress for large scans. Avoid turning ignored file volume into a permanent snapshot barrier. Restoration needs a durable planned effect and reconciliation, rather than weakening repository ownership protection. No tests run.

### L530 Git handle recovery has strict path, topology and schema requirements but no TTL

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/manifest.rs:20-30`, `src/manifest/worktree.rs:66-101`, `src/manifest/worktree.rs:152-212`, `src/worktree/lifecycle.rs:189-258`, `src/worktree/recovery.rs:131-186`, `src/manifest/snapshot.rs:71-111`.
- Behavior: Manifests accept exactly schema 1 under shared production codec limits, require UTF-8 absolute paths and reject trailing bytes. Worktree destinations must have a leaf identical to the validated name and reside outside the opened repository root and Git storage. Ordinary manifest reopening requires the original detached baseline HEAD. There are separate recovery functions for exact interrupted creation and for a previously trusted worktree's current detached HEAD; the latter preserves working changes and adopts the currently observed commit/tree as the recovered baseline. Snapshot refs and repository identity are revalidated exactly.
- Consequence: An advanced HEAD cannot use ordinary original-manifest reopening but does have an explicit current-worktree route. An in-repository .worktrees directory is unsupported by this adapter. Moving a repository changes its path-bound identity; old manifests do not automatically rebind. Git handles, worktrees and retained snapshot refs do not expire on a wall timer or disappear merely because a typed handle is dropped.
- Repair direction: Preserve explicit trusted recovery and binding checks, add intentional format/path migration when needed, and ensure higher callers select current-worktree recovery where appropriate. Do not mistake these durable handles for ephemeral provider contexts. No tests run.

### L531 Snapshot admission and clean reconciliation include ignored path state

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/snapshot/operations.rs:90-105`, `src/status.rs:227-252`, `src/reconcile.rs:49-60`, `src/reconcile.rs:110-155`, `src/worktree/lifecycle.rs:119-132`.
- Behavior: Snapshot creation requires the current complete status digest to equal the candidate's prior recorded status, in addition to matching detached HEAD and index tree. That digest includes reported ignored paths. Reconciliation defaults to disallowing ignored paths but permits an explicit allow_ignored choice. RequireClean removal refuses every reported status entry, including ignored paths; ForceRegistered is a distinct explicit effect policy.
- Consequence: New ignored paths between candidate and snapshot creation can invalidate the candidate even without a change to its staged tree. Ignored build/log artifacts prevent default clean classification and clean removal. This is a policy distinction, not evidence that files may be discarded automatically. Conflicts and attached topology remain explicit indeterminate states.
- Repair direction: Bind candidate content and observational dirtiness separately, define intentional ignored-content policy at callers, and retain exact registration/effect authority for destructive cleanup. No tests run.

### L532 Some Git effects lack an idempotent completed-cleanup recovery result

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/worktree/lifecycle.rs:119-185`, `src/snapshot/operations.rs:247-272`, `src/snapshot/support.rs:82-140`, `src/snapshot/quarantine.rs:33-69`.
- Behavior: Worktree removal validates the existing canonical root before issuing removal; retry after completed removal fails because the root is absent. Snapshot release first requires the retained ref to exist and match; retry after completed ref deletion fails reconciliation. Candidate/staging, restore, ref updates and worktree creation can also finish effects before later observation, output or manifest errors are returned. In contrast, snapshot quarantine explicitly recognizes its exact already-completed state, and interrupted worktree creation has a dedicated recovery route.
- Consequence: A crash or lost receipt after cleanup can leave callers with error guidance instead of a proven completed result. This adapter alone has no command ledger that resolves those cleanup outcomes; a higher-level durable caller may compensate and must be examined before claiming a live dead end. Removing identity checks would lose safety without establishing completion.
- Repair direction: Resolve cleanup through durable intent, expected identity and post-effect observation, distinguishing exact completed absence from unproven absence or replacement. Preserve the existing compare-and-swap and quarantine behavior. No tests run.

### L534 Managed networking requires finite connection and owner lifetimes

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/plan.rs:34-90`, `src/accounting.rs:44-98`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:92-148`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:19-27`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:28-33`, `src/canonical.rs:8-59`.
- Behavior: NetworkBounds requires positive connection duration and a positive proxy-owner duration at least as large, plus positive per-connection bytes and aggregate bytes at least as large. There is no None/unlimited mode. The owner stops accepting once elapsed time reaches total_millis, cancels workers and revokes its configured credential. Workers and upstream sockets install mandatory connection_millis read/write/connect timeouts and enforce elapsed connection accounting. Other ceilings are 1..1,024 accepted connections, 1..maximum_connections concurrent workers, 4..65,536 retained observations and 256 bytes..1 MiB headers. Canonical plans have a fixed 2 MiB bound checked after complete allocation.
- Consequence: Long-running authorized network work is terminated by a synthetic lifetime even when making progress. Persistent process/session ownership does not remove these separate proxy deadlines. This crate exposes caller-selected values, not the actual installed caller values; native sandbox callers still require complete reading. Plan bytes bind these values and currently provide no widening/renewal operation.
- Repair direction: Model absent execution deadlines directly, separate transport cancellation/progress from explicit authority expiry, and preserve recoverable quota/backpressure state. Do not substitute a very large integer for an unlimited lifecycle. No tests run.

### L535 Proxy acceptance quota counts rejected connections and never refills

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/owner.rs:103-136`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:38-74`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:143-147`.
- Behavior: The owner increments accepted before checking worker capacity or its lifetime connection allowance. Every busy response, malformed/unauthenticated request and failed worker launch therefore consumes connection allowance. Completed workers release concurrency slots but never replenish accepted. After the allowance is exceeded, all new sockets receive 503 while the listener keeps running until cancellation or owner expiry. Observations retain the earliest fixed number and drop every later record; no drain or rotation API releases capacity, and snapshots clone the complete retained vector.
- Consequence: Retry on a temporary busy response can permanently exhaust the proxy's lifetime admission quota. Waiting for workers does not restore admission. Later failure/closure/release diagnostics may be lost once the observation log fills. These count barriers are independent of the elapsed limits.
- Repair direction: Separate socket acceptance, rejected admission, active concurrency and authorized lifetime usage. Provide durable progress/backpressure and rotating observational storage instead of an unrecoverable counter ceiling. No tests run.

### L536 Proxy cancellation can block on unsupervised host calls and header reads

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/resolution.rs:29-46`, `src/credential.rs:292-299`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:41-48`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:142-160`, `src/proxy/http.rs:246-258`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:153-188`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:106-145`.
- Behavior: DNS resolution and credential acquisition are synchronous trait calls without cancellation. Request/response header readers perform one-byte blocking read_exact calls without observing the cancellation token. Shutdown and Drop cancel the token, then synchronously join the owner and its workers. Socket timeouts apply to individual calls, not a cancellation wakeup; header bytes arriving before each read timeout can keep parsing alive after owner cancellation. The owner's accept error returns through ? before its cancel/join/revoke epilogue, dropping worker join handles rather than resolving them.
- Consequence: Mandatory time values do not prove that shutdown can recover: blocked DNS/provider calls and continued header reads can hold joins. Increasing the timeout also increases the time before some workers notice cancellation. The early-error path violates the documented complete-owned-join contract in this layer; no live reproduction is claimed.
- Repair direction: Supervise cancellable host operations and owned socket shutdown, keep teardown on every exit path, and persist unresolved ownership instead of either detaching it or imposing another arbitrary deadline. No tests run.

### L537 Connection duration accounting uses different origins for different phases

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/worker.rs:41-67`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:91-118`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:104-172`, `src/accounting.rs:92-98`.
- Behavior: HTTP elapsed accounting starts after the entire client request header is read. DNS and connect occur before the next elapsed check, and upstream response-head reads do not consult that clock. CONNECT starts a new Instant separately inside each upload/download relay, excluding its earlier header/resolve/connect phases. Per-read/write socket timeouts reuse the complete connection duration. Elapsed accounting rejects strictly greater-than duration while owner lifetime stops at greater-than-or-equal.
- Consequence: The mandatory connection duration is neither a consistent whole-connection limit nor reliable cancellation. It can terminate a progressing transfer yet exclude expensive startup/header phases. A timer field is not evidence of a complete recovery contract.
- Repair direction: Remove implicit execution lifetimes and define observable phase progress and ownership cancellation consistently. If a user explicitly selects a deadline, represent its origin and scope once rather than restarting it per phase. No tests run.

### L538 Managed DNS and protocol compatibility can reject otherwise usable connections

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/resolution.rs:35-46`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:18-34`, `src/matcher.rs:103-151`, `src/plan.rs:206-233`.
- Behavior: System resolution revalidates every returned address and fails the whole result if any answer is denied. Connect sorts admitted addresses and tries only the first, with no attempt at the remaining admitted answers when that address fails. Matching reconstructs/clones the complete network rule contract for each request and resolved IP. UDP requirements are rejected because no exact datagram relay is implemented; managed requests support TCP only. Special-address and explicit-deny checks are retained security boundaries.
- Consequence: A mixed answer set or an unavailable first admitted address can block a destination even when another authorized answer is reachable. This is a compatibility/recovery limitation, not a reason to remove destination authorization. Repeated contract reconstruction adds synchronous work; no measured bottleneck is claimed.
- Repair direction: Preserve deny precedence and special-address authority while defining selection among independently admitted addresses and cancellable connection attempts. Supply an explicitly admitted datagram path where required. No tests run.

### L539 Upstream credentials require expiry and use counts, but exhaustion is silently omitted

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/credential.rs:103-183`, `src/credential.rs:250-272`, `src/credential.rs:301-317`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:142-160`.
- Behavior: CredentialLease requires positive uses and a nonzero wall-clock expiry, with no renewal or unlimited mode. It binds owner, plan, transport, port and host matcher and decrements before material acquisition or request encoding/write. The worker catches every consume error, including expiry/exhaustion/revocation/mismatch, and returns Ok(None), forwarding the request without the configured injection. Provider acquisition failure still consumes the use. Header names are at most 128 bytes and material at most 16 KiB, with injection-safe characters required.
- Consequence: An exhausted or expired proxy credential can appear to clients as an upstream authentication failure rather than the actionable ReacquireCredential error defined by the lease. Failed acquisition can exhaust all uses before any successful authenticated request. These leases are credential authority, not provider context/session TTL; their expiry must not be casually equated with context deletion.
- Repair direction: Make optional versus required credential injection explicit, propagate reacquisition state and retain exact pending use resolution. Keep host/owner/plan and header-injection protections. Define intentional authority renewal independently of synthetic transport lifetime. No tests run.

### L540 HTTP header effects occur before network byte ceilings are charged

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/worker.rs:50-76`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:91-104`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:176-201`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:175-186`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:215-228`.
- Behavior: CONNECT success, upstream request headers and final response headers are written before their byte charges are checked. Body relay charges before forwarding. Per-connection accounting mutates before the shared total charge, so total rejection can leave the local account charged for a chunk never forwarded. Aggregate budget is lifetime state with no refill. Discarded redirect bodies also consume it.
- Consequence: A byte-limit error can occur after an upstream request has already triggered an effect or after a success header was sent. Retrying that generic connection failure cannot by itself prove safe replay. Configured byte counts mix forwarded control bytes, discarded bodies and reserved/unforwarded chunks. These are not execution timers but can stop useful work.
- Repair direction: Reserve/resolve exact transmission accounting before effects and preserve uncertainty for requests whose remote outcome is unknown. Separate user-selected network budget from observational counters and connection backpressure. No tests run.

### L541 Proxy redirect and HTTP restrictions turn some normal responses into connection failure

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/http.rs:84-144`, `src/proxy/http.rs:185-207`, `src/proxy/http.rs:260-264`, `src/redirect.rs:15-54`, `src/redirect.rs:81-99`, `src/proxy/redirect_worker.rs:13-30`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:91-118`.
- Behavior: HTTP requests must use uppercase-letter methods and HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1; every request Transfer-Encoding is rejected, including chunked bodies. Only plain-HTTP absolute targets, origin form or CONNECT are supported. Headers are UTF-8, names at most 128 bytes, rewritten heads at most 1 MiB. Redirect targets are at most 8,192 bytes and the counter is u8 with no unbounded mode. Despite its documentation mentioning HTTPS, RedirectTarget::parse accepts only http://. The proxy always attempts to process a 3xx Location; RedirectMode::Deny returns an error rather than forwarding that response. Following also rejects body-bearing requests and methods other than GET/HEAD.
- Consequence: Ordinary HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, disabled internal following or redirected uploads can surface as EOF/failed connection instead of a response the client can handle. Named/header/count ceilings add compatibility barriers. Removing request framing validation indiscriminately would undermine protocol integrity.
- Repair direction: Forward ordinary redirect responses when internal following is disabled or unsupported, and define supported streaming/framing behavior explicitly. Preserve destination reauthorization for any internally followed successor. No tests run.

### L542 Proxy recovery records classify supplied facts rather than reconnecting owned sockets

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/recovery.rs:20-94`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:71-79`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:153-188`, `src/proxy/inherited.rs:32-40`.
- Behavior: ProxyRecoveryRecord is an in-memory checksummed value. This crate has no record encode/decode or attach/reopen operation that restores a ManagedProxy from it. classify accepts an observed owner and caller-supplied listener/worker facts; it does not inspect the recorded listener port, current plan or routing token. Absent listener/zero workers is AbsentClean only if released was already recorded; otherwise it is Mismatched. Live handles own process-local threads, cancellation tokens, sockets and non-clone routing material and cancel/join on Drop.
- Consequence: A checksum and LiveOwned classification do not establish exact live reattachment. A crash before recording released does not become a proven clean completion through this classifier. Higher native recovery adapters may provide observation/reconciliation and must be read before claiming a live failure. There is no durable same-context recovery implementation here.
- Repair direction: Bind recovery to real observed runtime identities and durable intent/completion, with explicit absent/unknown/replacement handling. Keep socket ownership distinct from provider context identity. No tests run.

### L543 Inherited listener handoff assumes a complete record from a stream read

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/inherited.rs:159-197`, `src/proxy/inherited.rs:200-283`.
- Behavior: A Unix stream channel sends a fixed record plus one SCM_RIGHTS descriptor. Receive requires one recvmsg to return exactly the complete record bytes and exactly one descriptor; a short stream delivery is rejected and received descriptors are closed. It does not retain a partial record for continuation. The receiver polls nonblocking every five milliseconds and observes explicit cancellation; proxy lifetime timing begins only after the listener is received and owner::run starts.
- Consequence: Stream segmentation is represented as an invalid handoff rather than resumable framing. A slow handoff has no implicit timer in this layer, which is consistent with explicit cancellation, but the returned endpoint remains absent until successful framing. Five-millisecond polling is cadence, not a session deadline.
- Repair direction: Define descriptor-bound stream framing with retained partial bytes or use a matching message-oriented channel contract. Preserve exact descriptor count, loopback and close-on-exec validation. No tests run.

### L545 Secret delivery requires finite expiry and use budgets and cannot renew an active lease

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/lease.rs:27-35`, `src/lease.rs:59-84`, `src/lease.rs:92-135`, `src/preparation.rs:34-47`, `src/preparation.rs:59-120`, `src/delivery.rs:170-205`.
- Behavior: Every secret lease requires nonzero remaining uses and a nonzero expiration timestamp. Expiry permanently changes its state before owner and execution scope checks, and successful delivery decrements its lifetime use count. There is no unlimited representation or renewal operation. Preparation permits at most 128 leases and reuses the timestamp captured when the preparation object was constructed. Material lookup occurs before delivery validates the live lease, and a file-staging failure does not return the moved lease for retry.
- Consequence: A continuing authorized execution can lose credential delivery solely because of these finite budgets; a delayed preparation can also check an old time. An incorrectly scoped attempt at or beyond expiry can change lease state. These are source-level behaviors; installed caller values and native recovery integration remain separate questions.
- Repair direction: Separate authority revocation from arbitrary lifetime budgets, support explicit unlimited or renewable authorized delivery, validate scope before state mutation, obtain the current time at the actual check, and preserve retryable ownership on staging failure.

### L546 Redaction fingerprint construction expands the entire secret before applying its count limit

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/material.rs:8-22`, `src/fingerprint.rs:51-75`, `src/fingerprint.rs:80-89`, `src/fingerprint.rs:116-133`.
- Behavior: Material accepts up to one MiB. Redaction construction hashes every sliding fragment of length four through 64, collects all hashes, sorts and deduplicates them, then rejects more than 65,536 unique fingerprints. For a one-MiB input, this constructs 63,961,124 fingerprint entries before deduplication. Each hash builds another temporary byte vector. Matching scans the fingerprint vector synchronously.
- Consequence: An input allowed by the material boundary can incur tens of millions of allocations and hashes, substantial memory use and sorting before a later rejection. No cancellation or progress boundary is provided. The expansion is derived from the loops, not a measured stress run.
- Repair direction: Define a redaction representation and algorithm whose construction and matching costs are bounded by the accepted material size; reject unsupported inputs before expansion or process them incrementally with cancellation. Preserve the security purpose of redaction.

### L547 Redaction expiry disables matching even while secret material may remain live

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/fingerprint.rs:39-44`, `src/fingerprint.rs:51-58`, `src/fingerprint.rs:80-89`, `tests/secrets.rs:119-128`.
- Behavior: A redaction set requires a finite nonzero expiration timestamp. At or beyond that timestamp, matching returns false. The test explicitly expects a previously matching secret to stop matching after expiry. There is no renewal or coupling to confirmed removal of delivered files and other material copies.
- Consequence: A timer can disable an output-protection check while a continuing execution or retained artifact still contains the secret. This establishes the local contract, not a confirmed installed disclosure; callers and delivery lifetime need to be traced together.
- Repair direction: Retain redaction coverage for the lifetime of material and outputs that can contain it, with explicit ownership and verified retirement instead of elapsed-time disappearance.

### L548 Failed file staging and destructor cleanup can lose ownership of secret artifacts

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/delivery.rs:178-205`, `src/delivery.rs:229-285`.
- Behavior: Staging creates a lease-named file exclusively, writes and syncs it, then adds it to the session only on success. If write or sync fails, an attempted removal error is ignored, leaving a possible partial file outside the artifact list. A later exact retry encounters the existing name. Explicit release retains failed removals for retry, but Drop discards release errors and destroys the owner object.
- Consequence: A partial artifact can survive without a retryable ownership record; process teardown can discard the only cleanup state. A finite lease does not solve this recovery gap. No injected filesystem failure or crash was executed during this audit.
- Repair direction: Journal ownership before creating artifacts, preserve cleanup failures durably, and reconcile exact existing artifacts on recovery and retry. Retain explicit idempotent release and restrictive file permissions.

### L549 Secret recovery classifies supplied metadata without reattaching the delivery session

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/recovery.rs:23-81`, `src/delivery.rs:170-205`, `tests/secrets.rs:177-202`.
- Behavior: The recovery record contains owner, lease, reference, execution digest and live/released flags with a checksum. Classification accepts a supplied resource-present Boolean and optional lease; it can classify a record as live with no supplied lease. The crate supplies no record serialization, session rehydration or exact live-file/path attachment. Absence is clean only when the stored record already says released.
- Consequence: These metadata checks alone cannot reconnect a restarted executor to its previous secret delivery or prove cleanup of an interrupted owner. The tests construct metadata and Boolean observations rather than performing native restart attachment.
- Repair direction: Persist recoverable ownership and exact native identities, reconcile interrupted creation and release, and rebuild the continuing session only from verified resources. Keep checksum and scope checks as integrity requirements.

### L550 Credential-store availability probing hides causes and blocks synchronously

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/store.rs:60-80`, `src/store.rs:95-146`, `src/store.rs:151-160`, `src/store.rs:226-232`, `src/reference.rs:1-86`.
- Behavior: Platform-store operations perform a synchronous availability probe using `store_status().is_ok()` before access. Probe failures collapse to unavailable/retry instead of retaining locked or denied causes, even though later keyring errors have more specific recovery classifications. Lookup retrieves and hashes all returned bytes before material-size validation. References bind a resource/version digest, but the persistent namespace is configured outside the reference. A repeated remove of a missing entry reports missing rather than completed cleanup.
- Consequence: A locked store can be presented as retryable unavailability, and a blocked native probe has no cancellation path in this crate. Namespace drift and late size rejection can prevent otherwise authorized credential access. Version-digest and owner checks are integrity controls rather than synthetic session deadlines.
- Repair direction: Preserve native failure causes, make host calls cancellable, validate admitted sizes before expensive processing where the backend permits, persist the effective namespace binding, and reconcile already-completed removal explicitly.

### L552 Patch preparation can leave a manifestless blocker and quarantine has only 100 names

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/transaction/apply.rs:62-103`, `src/transaction/apply.rs:114-147`, `src/transaction/storage.rs:20-36`, `src/transaction/recover.rs:39-69`, `src/transaction/recover.rs:298-334`.
- Behavior: The transaction directory is created and synchronized before final files are staged and before the first manifest is persisted. Root synchronization failure returns immediately; later preparation failures attempt cleanup but ignore its outcome. Exact retry rejects an existing directory. A manifestless directory is quarantined as indeterminate. Quarantine tries only the base name and suffixes one through 99, then returns a fencing error.
- Consequence: An interruption before the manifest exists can leave a directory that blocks retry and cannot establish safe completion from this crate's recovery contract. Repeated quarantine conflicts exhaust a fixed name budget. Successful installation exposes cleanup-pending status, but pre-mutation and restored failures do not expose ignored cleanup failure separately.
- Repair direction: Durably record transaction ownership and preparation state before creating effects, reconcile safe interrupted preparation, retain cleanup status on every exit, and use collision-resistant quarantine identities without a fixed lifetime name budget.

### L553 Patch cleanup removes the local completion evidence and repeated recovery fails on absence

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/transaction/apply.rs:139-147`, `src/transaction/storage.rs:114-121`, `src/transaction/roots.rs:29-38`, `src/transaction/recover.rs:31-38`, `src/transaction/recover.rs:273-283`.
- Behavior: Successful application returns an installed manifest but deletes the transaction directory when cleanup succeeds. Recovery first requires that directory to exist. Cleanup removes the directory before synchronizing its parent; a failed parent synchronization reports cleanup pending even though the directory can already be absent. Repeated recovery then fails root inspection rather than returning already-applied or already-cleaned.
- Consequence: Exact completion replay depends on a durable caller receipt outside this adapter. Local disappearance alone cannot distinguish completed cleanup from missing ownership, and a reported cleanup-pending result can lead to a retry that has no directory to inspect. Higher-level receipt integration must be assessed separately.
- Repair direction: Persist a compact completion/release receipt before retiring large staging data, and reconcile exact repeated cleanup through that receipt, including the removed-directory/unsynced-parent boundary.

### L554 Patch filesystem work is synchronous and has platform and exact-observation restrictions

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/transaction/apply.rs:150-171`, `src/transaction/apply.rs:188-210`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:34-85`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:102-146`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:189-228`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:295-347`, `src/transaction/roots.rs:41-72`, `src/line_endings.rs:25-80`.
- Behavior: Targets above the shared production file bound cannot be exactly observed for a patch. Symlinks, special nodes and nested repositories are rejected. Non-Unix executable-mode patches are rejected before staging. Same-device root validation is implemented on Unix; other platforms accept that check unconditionally and can fail later during rename. Full file reads/hashes, repeated pre/post/rollback observations, directory discovery, normalization, writes and synchronization run synchronously without cancellation or a progress cursor.
- Consequence: This path has no synthetic wall-clock deadline, but blocked filesystem I/O cannot be canceled through the API and an accepted multi-file operation has no incremental recovery progress interface. File-size and platform representation limits can prevent legitimate edits. Exact preimage checks, disjoint roots and unsafe-target rejection protect mutation integrity and must remain effective when limits change.
- Repair direction: Support scalable exact observation and durable incremental progress, expose cancellable host operations, and validate native volume/mode capabilities before effects rather than treating unsupported checks as successful.

### L556 Sandbox time limits are optional but six resource dimensions still require finite bounds

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox/src/resource.rs:53-147`, `src/resource.rs:150-201`, `src/process_policy.rs:5-14`, `src/process_policy.rs:65-92`, `src/terminal.rs:152-176`, `src/terminal.rs:267-291`, `src/reference/session.rs:160-184`.
- Behavior: `with_optional_time` represents absent wall and CPU bounds as zero on the canonical wire and skips their finite comparison. Memory, disk, output, handles, processes and concurrency still require positive finite quantities. Process policy separately requires a finite simultaneous process maximum and a denied/bounded descendant allowance. Terminal output also requires a positive finite byte budget. The reference usage API only adds usage in all dimensions; it has no release/decrement or gauge update for simultaneous resources. Untimed counters still reject arithmetic overflow. Reference accounting enforces contract limits rather than the smaller requirements.
- Consequence: Removing timers does not remove output/storage/capacity ceilings. Treating a simultaneous handle/process/slot count as cumulative charging would eventually exhaust a continuing session, although native callers must be inspected before asserting they use that reference pattern. The optional-time implementation is an existing repair and must not be mislabeled as a mandatory execution deadline.
- Repair direction: Preserve explicit absence of time bounds, give other policy budgets an intentional unlimited representation where authorized, and separate lifetime consumption from current/peak resource measurements with correct release and durable accounting.

### L557 Untimed sandbox plans still require backend wall and CPU timer features

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox/src/plan.rs:194-249`, `src/admission.rs:68-95`, `src/backend.rs:121-161`, `src/verified.rs:73-99`.
- Behavior: Feature derivation unconditionally inserts WallTime and CpuTime along with the other resource features, regardless of the optional time limits. Admission rejects any missing feature before preparation. Features also cover default filesystem, descendant and network denial; these controls are necessary even for effects the plan forbids. Admission compares declared support bits and kind, not actual runtime enforcement observations.
- Consequence: An otherwise sufficient untimed native backend can be rejected solely because it cannot enforce timers the plan does not request. Declared completeness is not qualification of operational liveness or restart attachment. This does not show the installed backend currently lacks those bits.
