Bundle defaults require positive finite limits: 4,096 entries per section, 1 GiB per entry, and 4 GiB total. The manifest independently hard-caps sections at 4,096, so increasing the public entry limit cannot raise the portable bound. Planning loads/verifies requested records and artifacts before its count rejection; it does not establish entry/total byte feasibility. Assembly writes earlier sections and artifact headers before late size/hash/total failures. Portable metadata has a separate fixed 32 MiB reader cap; sized reads allocate their vector before the total-byte check.
- Consequence: Large valid work can fail late despite successful planning and leave partial caller-owned output. These are per-record/export bounds rather than session expiry; their fixed format ceiling and configurable operational budgets are presently conflated.
- Repair direction: Version or stream large collections; preflight the exact serialized byte plan, publish completed output atomically, and expose resumable export cursors instead of forcing whole-export failure. Check remaining budgets before allocation. Source review only; no tests run.

### L622 Admitted causal history across revisions cannot be represented by the current portable bundle policy
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/causality.rs:35-67`; `src/bundle/plan.rs:94-119,206-238`; `src/freshness.rs:35-76`; `tests/admission.rs:137-176`; `tests/freshness.rs:27-89` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Admission requires causal parents to exist and have earlier journal positions; it does not require their revision to equal the child's. Bundle planning requires all records to be current against one supplied revision, every causal parent to be included, and all included records to share the same exact revision tuple. Explicit invalidation is durable and dominates drift; no elapsed-time TTL appears in this freshness implementation.
- Consequence: A valid current record citing an older-revision parent has no successful bundle selection: omitting the parent breaks ancestry, while including it breaks currentness/revision equality. This is a source-derived history/export incompatibility, not proof that the installed run hit this path. The ancestry test only uses one revision.
- Repair direction: Distinguish historical causal provenance from a present-tense authority assertion. Preserve and export historical ancestors with their original bindings while checking current authority only where required. Source review only; no tests run.

### L623 Evidence work repeats synchronous whole-history and artifact verification without a resumable work owner
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/admission.rs:35-75,93-127`; `src/sqlite/store.rs:81-104,196-216,274-289`; `src/bundle/plan.rs:125-177,206-238`; `src/bundle/assemble.rs:80-119`; `src/bundle/verify.rs:145-168,278-284` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Admission scans the checked export's artifact references and verifies artifact bytes before recognizing an exact retry. Bundle planning reloads records for freshness, verifies duplicate artifact references before deduplication, and linearly searches records for each frame. Assembly verifies each artifact again and then hashes its stream; offline verification similarly matches each frame against the full record list. The Read/Write interfaces provide no cancellation or durable cursor, and final EOF validation can block on a still-open stream.
- Consequence: Growing history and repeated retries can spend substantial time reading and hashing while producing no new durable result. EOF can wait indefinitely; this is an unowned blocking operation, not an artificial session deadline.
- Repair direction: Bind verified content to immutable digests and one transaction snapshot, index frames and artifact references, recognize durable retries before redundant work when safe, and persist cancellable phase/cursor progress. Source review only; no tests run.

### L624 Evidence startup holds a write transaction for a full catalog scan and has no quarantine reconciliation operation
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/sqlite/quarantine.rs:49-76,84-106,159-199`; `src/sqlite/row.rs:56-104,107-155`; `src/sqlite/store.rs:57-64` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Every open begins an immediate transaction, materializes every active identity, and fully validates each record plus normalized collections and artifact roots before commit. CorruptCatalog rows receive a digest-bound copy in quarantine and remain in the original table; load rejects any quarantined identity. This module exposes observation/count APIs but no restore or reconciliation operation. Malformed identity bytes fail the identity scan before individual containment; other scan failures abort startup.
- Consequence: Startup work grows with the entire catalog while holding the writer lock, interacting with L620's five-second contention failure. Quarantine correctly prevents corrupt evidence from being silently reused, but a repaired dependency does not itself make that identity usable again.
- Repair direction: Retain corruption checks and copied evidence, but make verified scan progress durable and bounded per transaction; implement explicit digest-checked reconciliation/rebuild ownership rather than a permanent unusable identity with an operator-only recovery label. Source review only; no tests run.

### L626 Projection storage repeats the five-second SQLite contention cutoff
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-projection/src/sqlite/store.rs:13-72,186-209`; `src/error.rs:84-97`; `src/sqlite/schema.rs:3-28` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Projection connections default to a five-second busy timeout with mandatory Duration configuration. Busy/Locked map to Retry while other SQLite errors map to CorrectInput, with their source retained. Versions, positions, counts, and generations ultimately must fit SQLite INTEGER even though the pure model uses u64; generation allocation only checks u64 overflow before persistence conversion.
- Consequence: Contention can stop startup/install at another artificial timer. Representation exhaustion is separate from elapsed-time policy; an i64 overflow is reported as corrupt-catalog/rebuild even when it came from a new otherwise valid pure candidate.
- Repair direction: Give the shared database owner cancellation-aware durable contention handling and classify representability separately from corruption. Source review only; no tests run.

### L627 Any journal advance forces an in-memory genesis rebuild rather than incremental continuation
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-projection/README.md:20-32`; `src/catalog.rs:124-155`; `src/rebuild.rs:45-55`; `src/replay.rs:75-129`; `src/fold.rs:44-94`; `src/sqlite/store.rs:80-125`; `src/agent.rs:86-119` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Startup compares against the exact final position/head and selects RebuildFromGenesis on any position change. Replay requires the complete contiguous export from position one, creates fresh state, folds all records, encodes the entire state, and computes another whole-state invariant encoding. Checkpoints bind digests rather than providing a typed state decoder or replay cursor. Candidate work exists only in memory until the final install. Each configured projection independently drives this path; this crate has no incremental catch-up, automatic startup coordinator, or cancellation/continuation API.
- Consequence: An interrupted or contended rebuild repeats old reads and computation from genesis; costs grow with retained history. Agent projection entries retain phase/counters/digests, not the complete context or reducer state needed to resume a turn. A valid derived checkpoint alone does not establish session reconnection.
- Repair direction: Persist an integrity-bound typed checkpoint and aggregate cursors, apply verified suffixes, and retain rebuild phase progress without changing the authoritative run/context identity. Source review only; no tests run.

### L628 Projection installation compares generation ownership but does not check that its candidate still represents the current journal
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-projection/src/sqlite/swap.rs:22-91,147-191`; `src/sqlite/schema.rs:3-28`; `tests/rebuild.rs:27-88` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Atomic install validates the candidate's own payload digest/count and compares only the caller's expected active generation. It checks no authoritative current journal position/head in the install transaction. A journal advance without a competing projection install leaves that CAS unchanged, so an older candidate can still become active; a later startup then asks for another genesis rebuild. All old generation payloads remain in SQLite, with no garbage-collection operation in this crate. Identical valid bindings are reused and a stale generation CAS rolls back atomically.
- Consequence: Busy active journals can repeatedly obsolete expensive rebuilds without a suffix catch-up plan. Repeated changed bindings retain complete duplicate derived payloads and grow disk usage. This is a consistency/work-amplification gap; no installed recurrence is claimed.
- Repair direction: Compare the candidate's authoritative journal binding at activation or atomically catch up to a verified suffix; retain the old active generation until success and reclaim only unreferenced derived generations under an explicit retention owner. Source review only; no tests run.

### L629 Malformed projection metadata bypasses the advertised reasoned rebuild plan
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-projection/src/sqlite/store.rs:80-125,157-209`; `src/catalog.rs:124-155`; `src/sqlite/swap.rs:178-191`; `tests/rebuild.rs:90-125` in the same crate.
- Behavior: plan_startup propagates load_active parsing failures rather than returning a rebuild reason. Invalid generation/position/count values or wrong digest lengths therefore return CorruptCatalog/Rebuild directly. A valid-length payload corruption does reach PayloadCorrupt and can be replaced. Reuse verifies payload bytes and schema/head/position bindings but does not independently reconstruct or bind the stored invariant digest and record_count; they can differ from the payload without changing that reuse decision.
- Consequence: An embedding caller that only handles RepairAction can stop startup instead of rebuilding a nonauthoritative catalog. Current tests qualify payload-byte corruption, not malformed catalog fields or inconsistent invariant/count metadata. The safety of authoritative journal data is not inferred from derived-catalog reuse.
- Repair direction: Normalize derived-catalog corruption into an explicit rebuild/containment plan, validate complete checkpoint metadata, and preserve original diagnostic bytes without treating projection corruption as a reason to repair valid journal history. Source review only; no tests run.

### L630 Global projection replay rejects a changed revision or unsupported historic family before an unrelated fold can proceed
- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-projection/src/replay.rs:83-99,133-182`; `src/artifacts.rs:124-129,175-179`; `src/journal_catalog.rs:120-138`; `src/authority.rs:118-143`; `tests/rebuild.rs:128-183`; `tests/rebuild/journal_fixture.rs:33-65` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Every projection checks all records against the frozen family/schema registry and forbids changing an aggregate's exact revision digest. The journal fixture can durably append such a revision change, which replay then rejects. Artifact folds ignore event payloads but still pass through these global gates. Typed payload checks occur in individual relevant folds; the generic catalog accepts registered framed bytes, and authority family 94 has no typed decoder here.
- Consequence: One incompatible historical record can prevent every projection rebuild, including projections unrelated to that family. Removing timers does not repair this history-compatibility barrier. Registry/header validity and typed replay/reducer validity are distinct contracts.
- Repair direction: Define versioned history migrations/decoders and explicit aggregate revision transitions, preserving exact immutable provenance; make the journal admission and projection replay contracts agree. Do not silently skip authoritative corruption. Source review only; no tests run.

### L634 Filesystem schemas impose whole-file and inline-mutation ceilings without ranged alternatives
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/input.rs:7-16,79-86,119-133,281-304,320-344`; `src/schemas.rs:7-38,61-75,78-118`; `src/decoder.rs:25-41,95-116`; `src/read.rs:220-232`; `src/catalog.rs:105-119` in the same crate.
- Behavior: fs.read requires a positive caller byte bound no larger than 48 KiB and has no offset, line range, chunk cursor, or artifact result. Discovery/search require depth 1..64 and entries 1..100,000; search additionally requires a literal no longer than 4,096 bytes, a per-file limit up to 8 MiB, total UTF-8 bytes up to 64 MiB, and matches up to 10,000. Mutation schemas accept content strings up to 65,536 bytes and present preimage sizes up to 8 MiB; patch arrays require 1..1,024 edits and compile against the patch crate's separate byte/operation ceilings. Paths have a 4,096-byte schema ceiling. Binary content consumes its base64-expanded string allowance. All descriptors impose 8 MiB output, 16,384-byte human/model output, and count fields of one, while explicitly selecting no timeout.
- Consequence: A legitimate source file larger than 48 KiB cannot be read with this tool, and a larger replacement cannot be supplied inline even when the lower patch engine supports more bytes. Raising the invocation timeout does not change these schema barriers.
- Repair direction: Provide exact digest-bound range/chunk reads and streamed/artifact mutation inputs with persistent cursors; distinguish envelope-sized chunks from limits on the total job. Source review only; no tests run.

### L635 Filesystem traversal/search loses progress at bounds and silently excludes some search scope
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/read.rs:239-324,327-365,377-395`; `tests/filesystem_tools.rs:50-60`.
- Behavior: Traversal materializes the entire selected subtree and returns an error at the next entry beyond the bound, discarding observed entries. It stops recursing at maximum_depth without a scope-truncated marker. Search first performs that whole walk, reads each eligible file, ignores binary and over-per-file-bound files, and only accounts UTF-8 bytes after the read. Total-byte or match overflow returns an error and discards all matches, with no continuation cursor. Preview text always contains the first UTF-8-safe 512 bytes of the line, even when the match occurs later. Case-insensitivity is ASCII-only. One no-follow symlink inspection failure rejects the entire traversal, as the test explicitly expects.
- Consequence: Broad code exploration may repeatedly redo the same reads instead of obtaining the next page; a no-match success does not establish absence in skipped/deeper files. The 64 MiB scanned-text allowance does not bound bytes read from binary files. Rejecting traversal/special nodes is an integrity boundary, but whole-job failure is a separate recovery choice.
- Repair direction: Return a truthful scope/skip summary and digest-bound continuation with retained partial results; budget actual I/O before reading and center match previews on the hit. Preserve no-follow guarantees while making unrelated unsafe entries separately reportable. Source review only; no tests run.

### L636 Filesystem result windows expose only the first 500 items and can still fail the canonical JSON ceiling
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/render.rs:10-11,59-111,118-147,188-226,243-261`; `src/dispatcher.rs:273-309`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/limits.rs:20-55`; `src/schema/canonical.rs:81-90,209-231,239-289` in the protocol crate.
- Behavior: Discovery and search render at most the first 500 entries/matches, truthfully label that window truncated, and supply no next-page token. Model/human renderings are summary sentences; file bytes, paths, and matches are in structured output. BoundedJson independently caps the whole canonical value at 256 KiB, depth at 32, members at 4,096, and each string at 64 KiB; custom limits can only narrow these ceilings. The renderer does not adapt the 500-item window to serialized size. A valid 48 KiB UTF-8 file of control characters expands past 256 KiB when JSON-escaped, and long path windows can also exceed the bound. Selected call output is checked after inspection/rendering. Oversized output becomes a generic protocol failure rather than an artifact or smaller recoverable page. Integer renderings saturate at i64::MAX rather than preserving larger exact u64 values.
- Consequence: Accepted read/traversal input can perform all its work and still return no usable result. Repeating the same request cannot expose item 501 or a too-large encoded file. Whether downstream model context includes the structured payload remains a composition question; the summary rendering alone does not contain file contents.
- Repair direction: Plan byte-sized pages against actual serialized limits, include a continuation/artifact digest, preserve exact numeric encodings, and verify downstream content delivery end to end. Source review only; no tests run.

### L637 Filesystem dispatch is synchronous, loses error distinctions, and retains candidate handoff only in its live object
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/catalog.rs:115-118`; `src/dispatcher.rs:71-78,132-174,201-228,273-303,311-357`; `src/error.rs:77-94,125-131`; `src/read.rs:377-390` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Descriptors now have no timeout, but ControlSet::NONE and synchronous start provide no pause/cancel/progress handle. Terminal timing uses the same pre-execution AuthorityInstant as start and completion. Workspace inspection preserves only a broad recovery class, discarding the underlying code/source; every apply_patch error is collapsed to Workspace/Reconcile. CorrectInput failures request NewAction with no recovery route; Reobserve/Reauthorize also require a new action. A successful MutationOutcome for the later candidate step is held in an Option on the live FsDispatcher and can only be taken once; no reconstruction API exists here.
- Consequence: Removing deadlines does not make long filesystem operations interruptible or restartable, and generic errors cannot tell a retry owner which exact state needs recovery. Losing the dispatcher loses this handoff value, connecting to the workspace candidate recovery gap already documented in L582. This is source behavior, not a fresh diagnosis of the live session.
- Repair direction: Preserve typed redaction-safe causes and durable operation/outcome references, distinguish retry/reobserve/reconcile semantics, measure real completion, and introduce cancellable phase ownership without adding a new lifetime cutoff. Source review only; no tests run.

### L643 Git observation and rendering ceilings have no continuation protocol
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-git/src/schemas.rs:9-24`; `src/input.rs:8-60,125-137`; `src/render.rs:14-16,30-140,146-200`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/result.rs:327-351` and the production JSON limits recorded in L636.
- Behavior: Git diff accepts at most 100,000 entries and 8 MiB of patch; history accepts at most 1,024 commits. The renderer then keeps the first 500 items, at most 32 parents per commit, and only the first 48 KiB of patch, with truncation flags but no next cursor or patch byte-range request. Rendering also has to fit the independent production JSON and prepared-call output bounds. Model/human renderings are summaries; fuller detail is in structured output.
- Consequence: A caller cannot page through a selected large result using this API. Long paths, subjects, or many-parent history can fail shared JSON construction rather than yielding a retrievable partial result. This is a source-derived composition gap, not a measured installed-session timeout or proof about downstream context delivery.
- Repair direction: Make complete immutable observations retrievable by cursor or artifact, with bounded individual pages and consistent envelope accounting. Preserve truthful completeness metadata without requiring callers to repeat the same prefix.

### L644 Git mutation can succeed before its terminal envelope is rejected
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-git/src/dispatcher.rs:117-173,185-233`; `src/dispatch_support.rs:23-45`; `src/render.rs:52-78`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/result.rs:327-351`; workspace restart dependency in L582.
- Behavior: Candidate/rollback dispatch consumes process-local optional mutation/candidate context, performs the workspace operation, renders, retains the resulting outcome, then builds the terminal result. Its preflight accepts 128-byte model/human limits instead of validating the eventual complete rendering. The rollback sentence `Restored {commit} as successor snapshot {snapshot}.` needs 129 ASCII bytes for a valid 64-character commit and 32-character snapshot, so that accepted bound can fail after the effect. Both result text lengths are checked by the protocol. Candidate result/JSON errors can likewise arise after publication.
- Consequence: The effect and successful reply are not atomic. A caller can see a protocol error despite an applied mutation, while continuation depends on the same in-memory context/outcome rather than a durable receipt adoption API. The 129-byte boundary is derived from source; it was not executed against a SHA-256 repository.
- Repair direction: Validate or safely render reply capacity before effect, and persist an exact-action result/reconciliation receipt that a replacement process can adopt without repeating the mutation.

### L645 Registered Git merge is permanently unsupported; errors do not provide progress or retry detail
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-git/src/catalog.rs:29-54,119-132`; `src/dispatcher.rs:145-150,185-233`; `src/read.rs:195-225`; `src/dispatch_support.rs:65-117`; `src/error.rs:1-121`.
- Behavior: The catalog advertises `git.merge` as lease-required history mutation, but both dispatcher and read implementation return Unsupported. That failure is Infrastructure/Workspace with NewAction and no recovery route. Workspace failures are broadly collapsed into reconciliation guidance; read retry guidance becomes reobservation. The catalog timeout is None and synchronous execution declares no controls or progress, recording the pre-execution authority instant as completion.
- Consequence: A planner can repeatedly select an advertised operation that cannot run or retry without useful causal detail. Long synchronous work has no local progress/control surface. These are capability/error-contract blockers; there is no Git descriptor execution deadline left to remove.
- Repair direction: Publish only supported operations or implement merge with durable authority and result recovery. Preserve actionable error/retry distinctions and report actual timing/progress for long observations.

### L647 Quality defaults now omit execution deadlines but retain finite output and protocol limits
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/catalog.rs:35-86`; `src/definition.rs:9-10,43-48,122-195,264-307`; `src/discovery.rs:124-143`; `src/plan.rs:43-92`; `src/dispatcher/run.rs:99-163`.
- Behavior: Both quality descriptors and automatically discovered checks use None for execution timeout. Explicit definitions can still select a positive timeout through the legacy constructor or optional-timeout constructor; the plan, definition, and call must agree exactly. Default discovered output is 8 MiB; descriptors allow 8 MiB total output, 32 KiB model/human renderings, 4,096 controls, three artifacts, and 65,536 progress events. Definitions require positive finite output/parser bounds, gate names at most 128 bytes, source labels 256, environment profile names 64, and checked C2 argv.
- Consequence: No synthetic quality default execution timer is present here. Output/representation ceilings and their cross-layer consistency still matter for long daily-driving checks, independently of user-selected deadlines and authority identity checks.
- Repair direction: Keep omitted execution deadlines omitted through composition; separate explicit user constraints and integrity bindings from retrievable output/progress retention capacity.

### L648 Quality discovery can reject the whole catalog and consume its retry inputs
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/discovery.rs:18,63-121`; `src/discovery/cargo.rs:7-34`; `src/discovery/just.rs:9-59`; `src/dispatcher/discover.rs:87-119,123-173`.
- Behavior: Discovery reads only root Cargo.toml and Justfile/justfile, each at most 1 MiB. Just scanning rejects more than 16,384 lines or 1,024 recipe names; it recognizes simple public zero-argument-looking headers, not the complete Just grammar. Every valid TOML table creates four all-targets/all-features Cargo checks. Duplicate names across explicit definitions, Cargo, or both Justfile spellings reject the whole catalog. The dispatcher takes its explicit vector before inspection and emits every complete check in one production JSON value; it retains the catalog only after terminal envelope success. That envelope has no cursor/artifact fallback and fewer allowed members than a 1,024-entry catalog needs.
- Consequence: A large or colliding surface can block even otherwise valid explicit checks, and retrying the same dispatcher sees consumed input. Unsupported discovery syntax is silently absent. Catalog shape/size failure is classified Protocol/Never rather than exposing the inspection/parser cause or a resumable result.
- Repair direction: Preserve explicit catalog availability and discovery diagnostics, reconcile names deliberately, use actual tool metadata for discovery, and serve large immutable catalogs in resumable pages before consuming retry ownership.

### L649 Hidden quality rendering truncation and progress caps can turn successful work into incomplete evidence
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/render.rs:9-39`; `src/execution/active.rs:18,76-100,129-140`; `src/execution/terminal.rs:35-78,82-105`; `src/result.rs:237-265,280-324`.
- Behavior: Output rendering escapes the full retained byte slice before limiting it. Its shared text helper silently truncates at 16 KiB, below the advertised 32-KiB rendering limit. An escaped output between 16 and 32 KiB is returned with Complete metadata despite that additional truncation; a larger chosen tail is truncated again at its end. Progress above the selected event count is discarded and marked progress_truncated. The quality decoder considers that flag incomplete evidence even if the process, complete artifacts, output parser, and success predicate passed, changing a success into IncompleteEvidence with fresh-action reauthorization guidance.
- Consequence: Model/human output can be misleadingly labeled complete, and a long successful check can be blocked solely by an informational progress count. The renderer also spends memory/time constructing bytes it will discard. These conclusions are source-derived, not an executed large-output check.
- Repair direction: Render only the requested window with accurate truncation metadata; make progress pagination/loss distinct from result evidence completeness so progress capacity cannot invalidate a proven successful execution.

### L650 Quality parsing depends on volatile event delivery rather than complete published artifacts
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/execution/active.rs:20-63,83-93,116-127,143-177,216-235`; `src/parser.rs:25-70`; `src/observation.rs:104-139`.
- Behavior: Selected parsers accumulate stdout/terminal bytes solely from process events in 256-event polls. Any sequence gap (including non-output events) or parser-buffer overflow permanently marks parsing incomplete. Complete output artifacts are published afterward, but the parser does not reopen those artifacts to recover missing bytes. The cursor, definition, parser buffer, flags, owner, and result are local memory. recover merely polls that same live object; there is no reconstruction/adoption constructor. With OutputParser::None the parser returns NotRequested immediately, while infrastructure/output completeness is still independently required.
- Consequence: A lagging consumer can classify a correct check as InvalidResult despite complete recoverable output, and replacing the quality execution object cannot reconnect its parsing context. Complete evidence must remain required; the blocker is the delivery-dependent way it is obtained.
- Repair direction: Parse content-addressed complete output or persist a resumable parser cursor/state, and implement durable same-operation owner/result adoption. Preserve failure on actually incomplete or invalid output.

### L651 Quality completion consumes ownership before fallible publication and envelope assembly
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/dispatcher/run.rs:179-207`; `src/execution/active.rs:143-177`; `src/execution/terminal.rs:35-78,107-130`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/result.rs:327-351`.
- Behavior: Launch takes the plan/backend/artifact store before the fallible gateway launch. Finalization takes the process owner before wait_and_publish, parser classification, result structure, timing, artifact references, and terminal-envelope creation. Only a fully built ToolResult is cached. Publication can return retained C2 terminal facts, but there is no durable local owner/result handoff for a later error. Preflight permits the spool bound to equal the entire call output bound, whereas the terminal protocol counts artifact bytes plus structured JSON against that same bound.
- Consequence: Completion at the allowed artifact-byte ceiling can fail on metadata headroom after the work and publication occurred. A subsequent poll/recover can encounter quality-owner-missing rather than recover the finished result or retry artifact publication. The capacity boundary and restart gap were inspected, not experimentally reproduced.
- Repair direction: Persist terminal facts and publication receipts before consuming ownership; reserve metadata capacity or account artifacts independently, and make final result assembly/publication retryable without rerunning the check.

### L652 Quality timeout/cancel/recovery classification can contradict its own decoder and remove recovery
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/observation.rs:123-139`; `src/execution/terminal.rs:133-199`; `src/result/contract.rs:9-67`; `src/result.rs:248-265,280-324`; `src/execution/failure.rs:11-55`.
- Behavior: Classification gives parser failure precedence, producing candidate InvalidResult when parsing is incomplete. Terminal failure construction separately gives TimedOut, Cancelled, or RecoveryIndeterminate disposition precedence. The decoder accepts those statuses only with candidate Infrastructure, so a timed-out/cancelled/indeterminate execution with incomplete parsing becomes MalformedOutput with Retryability::Never and RecoveryRoute::None. Process SelectBackend is also collapsed into reauthorization rather than retaining backend-selection guidance.
- Consequence: The adapter can manufacture an envelope its own consumer rejects, obscuring the original interruption and disabling the recovery route that the terminal initially carried. Removing default timers alone cannot repair cancellation/restart behavior.
- Repair direction: Derive structured outcome and terminal failure from one consistent classification, retain causal parsing/exit facts separately, and preserve the required recovery owner/route. Add producer-to-decoder cases for interrupted parsers.

### L653 Quality working-directory declarations are not enforced consistently
- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/definition.rs:98-113,228-232`; `src/acceptance.rs:92-107`; `src/plan.rs:43-92`; `src/dispatcher/run.rs:99-163`; `src/snapshot.rs:109-127`.
- Behavior: Acceptance hashes the definition's optional workspace-relative working directory. Plan compilation uses the independently supplied WorkingDirectory without checking that declaration; run validation compares argv, deadlines, and output but not the declared path. The clean-snapshot constructor instead requires the plan directory to equal the snapshot root exactly and be read-only, rejecting a valid directory within that snapshot. The plain constructor omits that extra clean-snapshot check.
- Consequence: An explicit subdirectory check can run in a different directory or be rejected by the stricter constructor, despite an acceptance binding that describes the declared subdirectory. Default Cargo commands also need their write locations configured outside the read-only snapshot; this audit does not assume any particular installed environment profile.
- Repair direction: Resolve the declared directory relative to the validated snapshot, bind that exact path/access into the execution plan, and validate the same relationship at every constructor and dispatch boundary.

### L658 Product workspace recent-list limits still remove discoverable choices; retained registrations are a different surface
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-product-state/src/workspace/selection.rs:9-19,29-54,61-156,239-273`; `src/workspace/profile.rs:92-115,201-247`.
- Behavior: Only 32 recent profiles are retained in the selectable/find-by-repository inventory. Eviction or removal preserves managed trusted registrations, without a numeric history cap, but drops direct-folder and restricted profiles from that retention surface. select/find/active search only recent entries. Retained registrations deduplicate by workspace identity or repository root. Validation requires registered roots/identities to be unique and performs pairwise scans. The 4,097-entry history fixture constructs retained records directly without validating the complete selection or effectful launcher catalog.
- Consequence: More than 32 chosen folders can lose their remembered selection/trust facts even though old runtime history may exist elsewhere. Managed registration history avoids that eviction, but cannot independently be selected from here; replacing a root's retained registration can remove references to an older lineage. This is not evidence that a provider session itself expires at 32 workspaces. Unbounded retained history also has quadratic validation work.
- Repair direction: Separate paged presentation recency from a durable complete workspace registry, retain all lineages required by active runs, and support lookup/adoption outside the presentation list.

### L659 Product-state shape gates are strict schema/identity rules rather than session timeouts
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-product-state/src/state.rs:11-70,121-209`; `src/provider.rs:101-132,136-228,268-290`; `src/provider/account.rs:10-61`; `src/provider/kind.rs:7-91`; `src/phase.rs:18-37`; `src/verified.rs:7-149`.
- Behavior: State accepts only schema 1 and denies unknown fields; no explicit version migration exists here. Bootstrap can only repeat/advance one phase. Generations saturate at u64::MAX rather than retaining strict advancement at that physical boundary. Provider routes are the closed 13 kinds, one direct profile per kind, 256-byte models/credential refs, 2,048-byte endpoints, 128-byte headers, absolute 32,768-byte account executable paths. Failover is explicit/default-off and requires two selected provider kinds. This pure state stores bootstrap/provider/workspace facts and no live-daemon readiness or process/context owner.
- Consequence: Unsupported versions and malformed canonical identities are intentional admission barriers, not artificial execution deadlines. The closed route shape limits multiple routes of one kind; schema changes require migration in composition. Persisting this document alone cannot prove durable runtime/context recovery. Generation saturation is a physical boundary, not a practical daily session timer.
- Repair direction: Preserve integrity validation and user failover consent, provide explicit schema/route migration, and keep runtime recovery ownership durably linked through its actual owner subsystem.

### L660 Account status can block foreground setup and misclassify infrastructure failure as sign-out
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-provider-onboarding/src/account.rs:14,55-76,84-115,164-177,180-229`; `src/account/windows_tests.rs:18-99`.
- Behavior: Account status uses synchronous Command::output with no local cancellation/progress surface and only checks the 64-KiB stdout/stderr cap after collecting both complete streams. Catalog observation probes Codex then Claude sequentially. Any unsuccessful status exit is SignedOut; launch failure, oversized output, or malformed Claude JSON becomes NeedsAttention without its actual diagnostic. Successful interactive login synchronously repeats status. Windows uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW and a Claude title opt-out; its regression exercises console isolation with a ten-second transport fixture.
- Consequence: A hanging/noisy status command can hold up the calling UI despite the nominal output bound, and an infrastructure failure can send the user through unnecessary login again. These observations do not justify adding a synthetic session deadline. The Windows ten seconds are fixture values.
- Repair direction: Make status discovery cancellable/asynchronous with incremental retention and explicit unknown/infrastructure outcomes, preserving credential-safe causal diagnostics and the existing console isolation.

### L661 Provider installation has no execution/download timer here; a size gate and nonpersistent effect handoff remain
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-provider-onboarding/src/install.rs:32-60,72-111,126-154`; `README.md:7-10`; `src/direct.rs:87-125`.
- Behavior: The approved installer download is HTTPS-only and at most 1 MiB by curl option and post-download metadata. It deliberately has no --max-time/--connect-timeout; run_command polls indefinitely at 100 ms. The README still claims download time limits. Installation uses a temporary script and ordinary child process with no durable adoption/cancellation state; on try_wait error it kills/waits that child, ignoring cleanup results. Direct credential publication precedes final non-secret profile validation; failed validation discards credential removal errors and returns the profile error.
- Consequence: The installer timer was already removed in actual code. Size rejection remains, and interruption or cleanup failure has no persistent repair receipt in this crate. Credential cleanup after profile rejection can leave an unpublished resource, distinct from provider authentication or session expiration.
- Repair direction: Align documentation with source; retain user cancellation and exact durable installation/credential-publication reconciliation without reintroducing synthetic time limits. Validate non-secret profile shape before effects and preserve cleanup failures.

### L662 Model onboarding blocks its caller while discovery owns an unreachable cancellation token
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-provider-onboarding/src/models.rs:14-29,32-125,128-143`; `src/direct.rs:59-74`; `src/error.rs:5-13`.
- Behavior: Synchronous model discovery creates a scoped thread/current-thread Tokio runtime and joins it. It uses a fresh CancellationToken that callers cannot cancel, with HTTP/metadata limits delegated to provider-core. Anthropic/Google requests select page sizes 1,000, and compatible discovery requires an endpoint ending exactly in /responses or /chat/completions. Unknown/manual-model handling is delegated to the caller; model discovery does not silently supply a bundled list.
- Consequence: Avoiding a nested async-runtime error does not make setup responsive or resumable; a slow discovery still blocks the calling thread with no UI cancellation handoff. Request shape/endpoint gates and provider-core bounds are distinct from inference/session lifetime. Pagination behavior remains owned by the separately reviewed provider-core discovery implementation.
- Repair direction: Expose asynchronous cancellable metadata discovery and retain exact errors/selected-model facts, with explicit paging where the provider advertises it. No model/provider request was sent during this audit.

### L663 Interactive daemon startup now has no synthetic readiness deadline, but readiness is only endpoint reachability
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app.rs:72-99`; `src/daemon.rs:54-78,121-191,193-255,258-278,372-386`; `README.md:3-6`.
- Behavior: The ordinary launcher explicitly uses DaemonSupervisor::without_deadline. Its optional constructor still permits a caller-selected readiness timeout; shutdown uses the same optional setting. Readiness is a socket/pipe connection without protocol/store/configuration negotiation. Sibling --version and the shutdown CLI run synchronously with Command::output, collecting full output without a local bound/cancellation. Spawned daemon ownership is detached from the terminal; successful readiness drops the Child handle while the daemon continues. Log files append indefinitely.
- Consequence: No default launcher startup timer remains here, despite older bounded-readiness wording. A connectable but unhealthy endpoint can pass this readiness predicate; synchronous probes or a stalled endpoint can hold up the async launch caller. This does not prove the installed session was hung at this boundary.
- Repair direction: Establish daemon identity/health and durable launch ownership through the protocol, move blocking subprocess work off the application event thread, and expose cancellation/progress without synthetic lifetime deadlines.

### L664 Immutable launcher snapshots can repeatedly replace the same shared daemon
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app.rs:77-116`; `src/daemon.rs:145-190,198-233,281-341`; `src/bootstrap/configuration.rs:73-87,354-368`.
- Behavior: Each launch retains one PreparedProduct/configuration snapshot throughout its recovery loop. The endpoint is derived from the stable installation/store identity. ensure_ready shuts down a reachable daemon whenever the applied marker differs from that snapshot's configuration path or the current daemon-file hash. It does not refresh/adopt current product configuration or negotiate the running daemon's actual generation. The marker is truncated/rewritten after endpoint reachability, contains a configuration path rather than configuration-content hash, and is not tied to an authenticated daemon process instance.
- Consequence: If two live launcher windows hold different configuration generations, each can replace the shared daemon when its TUI reconnects, producing repeat shutdown/reconnect cycles and repeated pressure on runtime/context recovery. A missing/partial marker can also trigger replacement. This is a source-derived causal scenario, not an observed reproduction of the user's current lockup.
- Repair direction: Give shared-daemon configuration reconciliation one durable owner, negotiate/adopt a compatible current generation, and coordinate required replacement with retained active-run/context ownership. A reconnecting presentation client must not repeatedly impose a stale configuration snapshot.

### L665 Direct-folder navigation and global tool allowlisting depend on the active presentation selection
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app/navigation.rs:39-58`; `src/app/navigation/tests.rs:75-106`; `src/bootstrap/configuration/folder.rs:8-22`; `src/bootstrap/configuration.rs:128-158`; `src/workspace_setup/managed/tests.rs:34-64`.
- Behavior: Navigation searches managed trusted registered profiles plus only the active profile. Inactive direct folders are rejected even when remembered; the regression explicitly expects that rejection. Generated configuration similarly includes only the active direct folder. The global C4 allowlist is populated solely when the active profile is Trusted; it is empty otherwise, although old managed registrations remain configured and navigable. Switching/forgetting choices publishes a new configuration generation.
- Consequence: A conversation in an inactive folder cannot reopen through this launcher surface, and browsing a restricted active choice can disable the shared C4 tool surface for other registered workspaces. This is a presentation/configuration coupling blocker, not a legitimate grant of another workspace's authority or evidence of a timer.
- Repair direction: Retain durable folder/workspace registrations needed by runs and resolve exact conversation scope independently of active presentation selection. Derive tool admission per authorized target while preserving explicit trust and target identity checks.

### L666 Product-state fallback can leave the next generation permanently occupied by corruption
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/persistence.rs:26-51,54-116,119-159,161-178,235-248`; `src/bootstrap.rs:44-49,71-98,179-198`.
- Behavior: Startup scans/sorts all generation files and falls back from invalid newer payloads to the newest valid state. It does not quarantine or reserve past those rejected generation numbers. A later change increments the recovered state by one; commit refuses an existing final filename with different bytes. Thus valid generation N plus corrupt N+1 permits fallback but blocks the next changed state at N+1. The recovery test uses a far-future corrupt generation and only reloads, so it avoids this immediate-successor collision. Pending publication is removed/restarted; mutable recovery files are replaced by truncating the final file in place. All generation files are retained, with unbounded reads/scans and no content-size check at this boundary.
- Consequence: Apparent fallback recovery can strand provider/workspace/bootstrap changes indefinitely. Interrupted mutable registration/settings replacement can leave a malformed final artifact. These are source-derived recoverability gaps; no corruption was injected into live product state.
- Repair direction: Allocate a new durable generation past every observed/reserved generation or quarantine conflicting candidates with explicit provenance, prove the next save after fallback, and atomically replace recovery files with synchronized receipts.

### L667 Generated provider ceilings are fixed by route kind rather than the selected model
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/bootstrap/configuration.rs:161-190,224-263,275-338`; `src/bootstrap/configuration/hosted.rs:13-46`; `src/bootstrap/configuration.rs:73-87`; `src/bootstrap/configuration/compatibility.rs:3-19`; `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/config/product.rs:8-23`.
- Behavior: Account/OpenAI routes receive 200,000 input and 64,000 output tokens; Anthropic 200,000/32,000; Google 1,000,000/65,536; compatible 200,000/32,000; hosted routes 32,768/4,096. Every profile sets 64 tools/eight parallel calls; inline media is 32 MiB or one byte and capability claims are assembled from route kind. Model catalog metadata does not set these values. Existing generated bytes must match exactly apart from one legacy timeout spelling. That retained provider_turn_timeout_seconds=600 field is accepted but ignored by current daemon policy, not an active deadline.
- Consequence: The selected model can be restricted by a hardwired conservative declaration or assigned capacities/features it does not have. Hosted 4,096-token output is a request-shaping ceiling independent of actual provider capacity. Arbitrary edits to generated ceilings fail immutability checks. The ignored legacy timeout must not be misreported as a current limiter.
- Repair direction: Retain discovered/explicit model capacity and supported features as versioned provider facts, distinguish user policy from provider capacity, and preserve correct no-timeout compatibility during migration.

### L668 Workspace selection can silently fall back from current-directory errors or regenerate forgotten lineage
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/workspace_setup.rs:18-38,103-159,211-246`; `src/workspace_setup/discovery.rs:26-64,86-119,123-137`; `src/workspace_setup/managed.rs:47-69,73-161,166-235`.
- Behavior: An explicit path fails visibly, but implicit current-directory discovery errors are ignored before reusing the stored active workspace or prompting. A discovered current folder/repository supersedes that active choice. Exact root+identity lookup searches only recent profiles; a miss creates fresh random project/workspace/resource/environment IDs. Git trust creates or recovers a detached managed worktree at the selected HEAD; direct folders retain the selected root. Health errors collapse to NeedsRepair. Automatic advanced-baseline refresh rewrites the registration before persisting the new profile/digest; registration replacement is in-place truncation.
- Consequence: A discovery error can select an older workspace without its actual cause, and a forgotten/evicted folder can receive a new lineage rather than adopt its existing run identity. Interrupted registration refresh can temporarily mismatch the durable profile/configuration and inhibit reopening. The managed Git copy is an explicitly disclosed product choice; this audit does not identify the live process cwd from source alone.
- Repair direction: Preserve discovery diagnostics and exact requested scope, resolve existing durable lineage outside the recent list, and make registration/profile/configuration refresh one recoverable publication protocol.

### L669 Provider setup can disable durable routes on transient status failure and block even offline startup
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/provider_setup.rs:24-31,91-153,184-234,237-287`; `src/provider_setup/models.rs:65-127`; `src/provider_setup/connection.rs:6-76`; `src/provider_setup/direct.rs:21-42`.
- Behavior: Every ordinary launch synchronously probes both account tools before checking prior setup/offline choices. NeedsAttention follows sign-in repair; declining or failing to restore readiness removes the route from the persisted enabled set and can choose another default/disable failover. A thrown login error instead exits startup. Retained model IDs are reused, and catalog failure permits an explicit manual model ID. Direct credentials are stored before the multi-provider selection is committed; cancelling later setup/test/publication has no enclosing credential-publication receipt. Settings remove replaced credentials even while old immutable configurations remain. Connection testing joins a blocking worker and has no caller cancellation handle.
- Consequence: A slow unused account probe can block direct-only/offline launch. Temporary status failure can become a durable route/configuration change, feeding the shared-daemon replacement behavior in L664. Deleting an old key can prevent continuation of older route generations; cancelled setup can leave an unpublished key reference. Explicit failover consent and manual model selection are legitimate user choices, not synthetic deadlines.
- Repair direction: Separate observed health from retained route intent; allow presentation/offline launch independently of optional probes, persist exact setup/publication ownership, and retain credential references while active durable generations require them.

### L670 Optional startup update discovery remains on the critical launch path without cancellation or durable download continuation
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app.rs:72-79`; `src/update.rs:13-44,85-118`; `src/update/release.rs:57-83`; `src/update/download.rs:15-107,125-172`; `src/update/install.rs:9-78,90-120`; `src/update/process.rs:18-108`.
- Behavior: Default-on cached release discovery is awaited before workspace/provider setup or TUI entry. The six-hour interval suppresses update polling; it does not expire sessions. HTTP clients configure no explicit timeout/cancellation here; release/checksum bodies are read completely before the 64-KiB/exact-hex check. Archives stream with a 1-GiB cap, but retry deletes the same release staging directory rather than resuming and has no update lock. Extraction/native install/version check explicitly pass None to the optional-deadline process helper. Its stdout drains with bounded retention but joins until EOF; a descendant holding the pipe can prevent return. Windows defers update into an untracked helper that waits for the parent PID and verifies only the CLI version.
- Consequence: An optional network operation or helper can hold up daily startup, and interrupted/repeated updates lose download progress or collide in staging. The source contains no active synthetic default updater execution timer; removing timers does not provide UI responsiveness, cancellation, or durable continuation automatically. Platform/architecture and exact release-tag admission remain separate packaging gates.
- Repair direction: Run optional discovery outside launch-critical work under a cancellable owner, persist resumable download/install receipts, coordinate staging ownership, and verify completion of the complete installed application/daemon pair.

### L671 Hidden credential input has a smaller cap and an incomplete terminal-mode acquisition rollback
- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/provider_setup/direct.rs:19,108-178,181-199`; `src/terminal.rs:34-63`.
- Behavior: Credential entry rejects more than 16 KiB and embedded pasted controls before the lower credential-store API. RawInputGuard::enter enables raw mode and bracketed paste, then flushes stdout before constructing the guard. A flush error returns without a guard destructor or explicit rollback, unlike the preceding bracketed-paste error path. Normal guard drop attempts cleanup but discards cleanup errors. Ordinary prompt cancellation/EOF exits setup and is not an execution lifetime deadline.
- Consequence: An acquisition failure can leave the terminal in raw/paste mode, which can look like a locked-up interaction. This was found in source; it is not established as the cause of the user's current session symptom. The credential capacity is a selected input bound, not provider session expiry.
- Repair direction: Construct ownership immediately after raw-mode acquisition and unwind every later failure, retaining cleanup diagnostics when restoration fails. Keep explicit user cancellation distinct from session expiration.

### L672 CLI default deadlines are removed, but interactive launch ignores supplied session and timeout options

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/args.rs:18-85,216-258,366-389`; `src/args/types.rs:17-20,70-76`; `src/runner.rs:22-26,52-66,145-198,200-251` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Parsing starts with no timeout. Event count is optional; its default flow-control window is 64. A user-supplied positive timeout remains supported, accepts the entire u64 range, and is later added to an Instant without a checked-add path in shutdown. Open/resume forward endpoint and repository/run selections but do not forward `--session` or `--timeout-seconds`; zero-argument invocation is a separate launch path. Update/settings enforce terminal requirements. Completion lists omit the runs command family.
- Consequence: These sources do not establish a remaining default CLI execution deadline. They do establish silently ignored interactive session selection and timeout settings, and an explicit huge-duration overflow risk. Whether the launcher/TUI chooses the correct durable run/context is separate from parsing a session option. Exact identities and candidate confirmation protect integrity and are not time limiters.
- Repair direction: Express interactive target/session policy in the launch interface and reject unsupported combinations; use overflow-safe optional deadlines for explicit caller choices. Keep default work lifetime unbounded. No tests run.

### L673 CLI event watch exits on disconnect or history gaps and does not durably resume delivery

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/events.rs:27-88,91-146,201-243`; `src/output.rs:16-55`; `src/runner.rs:68-80`; `src/operation.rs:177-244,260-264`; `src/id.rs:37-53`; `src/error.rs:63-69,127-145` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The event loop reads indefinitely and exits on any read/heartbeat error or gap, even when snapshot acceptance was requested. Deduplication stores only one negotiated window of IDs in memory; count and subscription state are also volatile. The CLI exposes start/session and event cursors in output but saves no resume receipt or cursor. New invocations generate new request identities. Writes/flushes to stdout execute synchronously on the same current-thread runtime before acknowledging delivery; a blocked output sink prevents further event, heartbeat, and Ctrl-C selection progress. Submit reads envelope/payload files fully before negotiated-bound validation. Structured remote recovery details are collapsed into a message/category.
- Consequence: Durable server history and the lower client API do not by themselves make this watcher or command invocation reconnect to its original operation. An indefinitely blocked output sink is a progress blocker with no synthetic time limit involved. A cursor gap is terminal here rather than an explicit snapshot/replay transition. This is source-derived behavior, not a reproduction of the user's running TUI.
- Repair direction: Give subscriptions and effect requests persistent identity/cursor receipts, reconnect/reconcile them without redispatching effects, and separate output backpressure from connection liveness. Bound file ingestion before allocating it and preserve typed recovery information. No tests run.

### L674 CLI artifact transfers lose resumable progress and output replacement has a destructive failure gap

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/artifact.rs:54-91,112-198,211-258,278-319,322-378,381-385`; `src/args/artifact.rs:74-105` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Download/upload allocate fresh transfer identities; chunk offsets, ordinals, digests, temporary filenames, and request identities live only in the invocation. Disconnect exits without reconciling the transfer. Receive errors remove the partial file and ignore removal errors; no remote cancellation is attempted. A publication error instead leaves an unrecorded part file. Upload hashes the entire input, reopens it, sends each chunk under a fresh request identity, and checks size only afterward; server digest verification remains necessary. Default upload chunk size is 64 KiB, constrained by the negotiated chunk maximum; these are transport framing bounds, not work TTLs. Forced output publication removes the previous output before fallible rename; non-force existence-check/rename is not an atomic no-replace operation, and directory sync is absent.
- Consequence: The resumable protocol cannot resume this CLI invocation without a retained transfer receipt; interruption repeats I/O and may strand server state. A rename failure after forced deletion can lose the user's previous output. Integrity checks on bytes and digest should remain; the missing persistent transfer/publication state is the blocker. Source-derived, no failure injected.
- Repair direction: Persist transfer/source digest/offset/temp publication state, reconcile an exact transfer after reconnect, and publish with atomic platform-appropriate replace/no-replace plus directory durability. Preserve partial verified data through recoverable failures. No tests run.

### L675 CLI terminal stdin buffers until EOF and terminal following has no reconnect state

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/terminal.rs:21-82,83-159,162-198,210-236,239-250,353-360`; `src/output.rs:35-47,74-110` in the same crate.
- Behavior: File terminal input streams negotiated chunks, but stdin is read to EOF into one unbounded Vec in a blocking task before any bytes are transmitted. An open stdin producer therefore prevents initial input indefinitely. Output follow stores stream state only in memory and exits on disconnect, unavailable output, or sequence validation failure. Ctrl-C exits without issuing an explicit detach/cancel. Attachment IDs are printed, but there is no cursor resume command or durable receipt here. A single sanitizer spans all streams, removes control strings until their terminator, and decodes each safe chunk lossily; split UTF8 and an unterminated control string can distort/suppress human output. Resize accepts the full u16 range even where native backends later narrow dimensions.
- Consequence: Input can appear frozen despite no execution deadline, and a live process cannot automatically restore its original output observation after connection loss through this CLI path. It correctly warns that unavailable output does not prove termination. Native ownership recovery and output replay must be established separately.
- Repair direction: Stream stdin in bounded chunks while serving heartbeat/cancel control, retain attachment/offset/sequence receipts, and reconnect against an authoritative stream disposition. Preserve incremental UTF8 and independent stream sanitizer state. No tests run.

### L676 Product-run CLI executes candidate commands without a persistent process owner and accumulates all list pages

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/product_run.rs:46-64,72-137,140-181,185-212,231-258`; `src/runner.rs:68-80`; `src/product_run/presentation.rs:14-44,69-126` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Runs list increments an offset, requests pages until a short page, and retains every result before output; no stable history snapshot or streaming pages are used. Local candidate execution synchronously recomputes a digest then calls Command.status inside the current-thread async runtime, with inherited I/O and no independent cancellation, process receipt, or owner reconciliation. No timeout is added. Accept/commit legality and optional unqualified-digest confirmation are checked in separate queries, then the mutation request contains only run ID and action; the confirmation digest is not carried into that request.
- Consequence: Large/changing history can delay listing and consume unbounded client memory. A long-running candidate command blocks client runtime progress and is outside the daemon-owned durable process recovery contract. CLI confirmation alone does not bind the subsequent server mutation to the candidate observed; whether server serialization independently prevents that race needs the protocol/daemon evidence. Candidate identity checking is necessary integrity, not a synthetic limiter.
- Repair direction: Stream stable run-history pages and route candidate execution through a durable process owner with explicit cancellation/reconciliation. Carry candidate identity/expected operation generation in exact mutation requests rather than relying on a pre-request check. No tests run.

### L678 Embedded workflow creates synthetic acceptance obligations even without elapsed deadlines

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/skills/independent-reviewer.md:3-27`; `skills/maintainable-developer.md:3-19`; `workflows/production-engineering.md:3-13,120-162`; `skills/repository-architect.md:1-8`; `README.md:128-157` in the same crate.

It applies many domain-specific evidence rules to every run with a proportionality clause. These are model instructions; this read alone does not prove that every item is a deterministic host gate. README documents 48-turn/512-tool segments and continuing fixer/reviewer cycles rather than a terminal cycle ceiling.

Pagination must prove progress, but a universal finite total-page rule is different from rejecting repeated cursors or caller-selected cancellation. Request-specific correctness, exact effects, actual requested tests, and dependency compatibility remain necessary; a prompt-only style rule should not silently expand a small task into unrelated restructuring.

### L685 Exact command retries require original request and correlation identities, which a fresh CLI invocation cannot supply

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/command/binding.rs:138-190,236-269`; `src/command/idempotency.rs:114-135,146-172`; `src/command/result.rs:99-105,148-165` in that crate; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/operation.rs:190-205`; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/id.rs:37-53`.

Matching session/actor/key with a different digest is a conflict. A new CLI invocation generates fresh request/correlation identities even if the user supplies identical command files, session, and idempotency key; its grammar offers no original request/correlation option. Result replay preserves the original request ID; this result is explicitly not a durable C0 receipt.

The binding protects effect integrity, but lack of a durable complete request receipt makes the protection a practical reconnect blocker.

Separate durable operation identity from transient connection correlation if the revised contract deliberately permits that, without weakening duplicate-effect protection. No tests run.

### L686 Pure idempotency window has a 4096-entry production ceiling and explicit oldest retirement

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/limits.rs:39-53,92-118,215-225`; `src/command/idempotency.rs:84-112,114-135,146-206` in the same crate.

There is no storage spill, pagination, or restore constructor in this type. Recording the same digest again returns AlreadyRecorded without checking equality of the supplied final result. This is a reusable pure contract; its use in the installed daemon must be established at callers, not inferred from its name.

A framing collection bound should not become a durable session's cumulative work quota. This read does not assert that the user's live daemon uses this pure window as its only receipt store.
- Repair direction: Store durable operation receipts independently of bounded in-memory caches and page them for lookup. Retire only through an explicit archival/tombstone policy that preserves duplicate-effect semantics; validate conflicting final facts. No tests run.

### L687 Artifact transfer protocol conserves bytes but has no resumable interrupted phase or restoration API

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/artifact/metadata.rs:70-94,138-161`; `src/artifact/state.rs:98-154,178-235,238-270,273-333`; `src/artifact/verified.rs:7-65` in the same crate.

Chunk/media/detail limits are selected by negotiated/caller framing; declared artifact total is u64, not a hardcoded goal byte quota.

### L688 Heartbeat and shutdown contracts contain no clock-based liveness or six-step execution deadline

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/daemon/heartbeat.rs:15-19,38-85`; `src/daemon/status.rs:20-31,41-64`; `src/daemon/shutdown.rs:117-142,183-209,261-370`; `src/limits.rs:39-53` in the same crate.

Neither six steps nor a wall-clock cutoff is built into this pure contract.

### L691 Product controls are not fenced to the observed candidate or operation generation

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/product/control.rs:55-76`; `src/product/operation.rs:190-221,255-266`; `src/product/snapshot.rs:29-69,134-151`; `src/product/settlement.rs:24-47`; `src/product/phase.rs:72-88` in the same crate; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/product_run.rs:72-137`.

### L693 Model catalogs and product observations have whole-response capacity boundaries without pagination at those DTOs

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/product/models.rs:6-7,23-33,133-148,167-197`; `src/product/snapshot.rs:35-54`; `src/doctor.rs:9-10,77-92,123-137`; `src/doctor/tests.rs:31-67`; `src/envelope/response.rs:65-149` in the same crate.

### L694 Closed application envelopes lack explicit artifact failure and stream-offset restoration messages

### L695 Default protocol recovery advice does not establish safe restoration of the original operation

### L697 Pure terminal attachment state has no saved-position restoration or replay admission
