The public receipt lookup only searches the C0 operation/archive; this path does not reconstruct the missing C0 receipt from the installed C1 transaction.
- Consequence: if the patch succeeds and final control publication fails, an exact retry can encounter the now-changed initialization preimage before reaching lower-layer consumption, while receipt lookup still returns absent. This preserves against blindly reapplying an effect but leaves successful authorized work without its completion acknowledgment.
- Repair direction: journal the cross-layer initialization intent and reconcile the exact installed C1 manifest into the original C0 operation receipt before any new proposal validation. Preserve owner, revision, action and proposal fingerprints. No tests run.

### L752 Review pages recompute the complete candidate and require execution eligibility

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench/review.rs:199-234,261-321`; `src/product_run/workbench/review/projection.rs:12-72`; L718.
- Behavior: each comment page loads the entire control record, takes the shared run-record read lock, requires may_start_execution, hashes the live candidate, parses the whole snapshot diff, and repeats all diff files plus two evidence states. Only comments are sliced. One stale/malformed projection rejects the page; comments preserve exact anchor digests and distinguish stale/dismissed/addressed state.
- Consequence: a nominally read-only review depends on execution-admission state and complete repository work under the record lock. More diff/history grows per-page work and single-frame pressure; paging comments does not page the candidate. Exact current-anchor checks protect against applying feedback to changed source and must remain.
- Repair direction: use a verified immutable candidate/diff observation with independent read eligibility and paged source coverage; require exact current fencing when mutating or starting feedback execution. No tests run.

### L753 Accepted review feedback can lose its execution handoff and exact retry does not restore it

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench.rs:120-150,157-202`; `src/product_run/workbench/review.rs:81-196` in the same crate.
- Behavior: the ordinary command commits AddReview/RebindReview to C0, then calls resume_feedback only for a fresh accepted receipt. Handoff can subsequently reject active workspace/operation state, fail adapter resolution or fail run-record persistence. An exact retry returns the existing C0 receipt early and never retries that handoff. Before persistence, resume_feedback replaces cancellation handles, mode, snapshot, progress (with defaults) and settlement in memory, with no rollback in this function.
- Consequence: a user can receive a handoff error after their feedback was durably accepted; retry can then acknowledge the feedback without starting its intended work. A failed save can leave an in-memory queued projection without a spawned owner. Starting feedback also resets aggregate progress rather than retaining the prior attempt base.
- Repair direction: persist a resumable feedback-execution handoff with the original command identity, reconcile it on both fresh and duplicate receipt paths, and commit/rollback the run transition before spawning. Retain explicit feedback modes and current-candidate checks. No tests run.

### L754 Ordinary workbench error mapping discards causes and labels storage failures as backpressure

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench.rs:298-322,367-390`; `src/product_run/workbench/images.rs:23-29`; `src/product_run/workbench/files.rs:86-128`; `src/product_run/workbench/folder_mutation/init.rs:14-46,90-97` in the same crate; L741.
- Behavior: control I/O/journal errors map to Backpressure with no diagnostic; corruption/runner/workspace errors map to NotReady except Reobserve, and image daemon errors collapse mostly to NotReady. File source/model failures similarly collapse to identifier/feature errors. A single synchronous mutex serializes all control operations, including full archive scans and authorized folder mutation.
- Consequence: ordinary user flows can receive pressure/retry instructions for persistent storage/corruption/authority failures, making repeated reconnect/read/retry actions look appropriate while the cause remains unresolved. Shared-owner blocking can affect independent conversations. These mappings are distinct from the more structured ProductRunServiceError path.
- Repair direction: preserve typed recovery ownership, exact operation receipt and full cause reference; separate transient admission pressure from unresolved durable state. Keep exclusive serialization where required but perform verified projections and long I/O outside progress-critical mutex scopes. No tests run.

### L755 Improvement backfill is whole-history work and its evaluation prompt still prescribes a bounded budget

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/improvements.rs:14-75,83-134`; `src/product_run/improvements/store.rs:178-222,260-280`; `src/product_run/improvements/evaluation.rs:13-44,98-181,188-240` in the same crate.
- Behavior: every inbox action first loads the entire existing inbox and scans every same-workspace run under run/store locks. Candidate reads allocate complete SQLite JSON before checking MAX_STATE_BYTES; every inbox reconstructs all candidates, including dismissed ones, with no page cursor. Evidence summaries are truncated to 4,096 bytes. SQLite uses a five-second busy timeout. Explicit evaluation serializes all launches, reads/parses the entire target Cargo.toml, queues each evidence source sequentially and ends its directive with 'Use the normal bounded run budget.'
- Consequence: growth increases synchronous collection/projection work and can hide detailed original failure evidence. The SQLite wait is a storage contention policy, not provider context lifetime, but its failure surfaces through a generic inbox internal error. The prompt retains a synthetic budget expectation even though current execution defaults may have removed that budget. Failure/cycle>=3 collection only suggests investigation; it does not stop work.
- Repair direction: page and incrementally backfill verified observations, retain complete source evidence references, expose cancellable contention recovery and remove obsolete budget instructions consistently with actual run policy. Keep evaluation explicitly authorized and untrusted observations inert. No tests run.

### L756 Improvement schema handling quarantines old state without a resumable migration transaction

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/improvements/store.rs:121-137,283-336`; `src/product_run/improvements/store/tests.rs:114-163` in the same crate.
- Behavior: schema 1 is renamed into improvements-quarantine and replaced with an empty schema-2 inbox; other nonzero unsupported versions fail open. Quarantine moves SQLite sidecars one by one before the main database, then syncs directories and writes a synchronous diagnostic. This function stores no move intent or recovery cursor. The fixture covers successful quarantine and retained legacy bytes; Windows directory sync is inert.
- Consequence: a failure between renames can leave a partially moved database/sidecar set; successful quarantine preserves files but does not expose their suggestions/evaluation reservations in the current inbox. A future schema remains an explicit compatibility blocker. Clean reopen coverage does not prove interrupted migration repair.
- Repair direction: retain a durable migration/quarantine manifest and reconcile every database/sidecar move before opening the successor store; offer evidence-grounded legacy recovery. Never reinterpret unknown schema bytes as current authority or discard old state. No tests run.

### L757 A suggestion has only one durable evaluation reservation across all future attempts

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/improvements/store.rs:139-175,230-258`; `src/product_run/improvements/evaluation.rs:46-97,157-173`; `src/product_run/improvements/store/tests.rs:36-79` in the same crate.
- Behavior: candidate identity hashes normalized proposal plus workspace, without harness/source revision. Once evaluated, evidence freezes. Reserve returns the original run/conversation when actor, target and provider IDs match, even if a new run ID was supplied; changing those owners/selection is rejected. Evaluation replays deterministic prepared commands and StartExecution for the original identity.
- Consequence: exact replay prevents duplicate launch, but the same suggestion cannot express a later separately authorized evaluation after a failed/finished attempt or a harness revision. A new requested run identity is silently replaced by the first reservation. This is a permanent attempt-identity restriction rather than an elapsed timer.
- Repair direction: preserve the immutable first evaluation receipt while modeling subsequent explicitly authorized evaluations as separate attempts fenced to source/harness revision. Keep duplicate retry resolution and frozen evidence for each original attempt. No tests run.

### L759 Formal readiness predicates prohibit diagnostics while startup remains incomplete

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/verified.rs:58-87,89-131,135-179,189-228`; L731.
- Behavior: the verified finite model admits mutations only in ReadyReadWrite and diagnostics only in ReadyReadWrite, ReadyReadOnly or Draining. Starting and Unavailable admit neither. Startup transitions must follow the exact fixed phase sequence. The executable wrappers refine those enum predicates; the proof does not model I/O progress, native supervisor ownership or restart adoption.
- Consequence: while long recovery remains Starting, this admission contract provides no diagnostic surface to explain progress or the particular stalled phase. Proving exact phase ordering is distinct from proving startup eventually completes or preserves an active context. Integrity readiness gates must remain even when elapsed limits are removed.
- Repair direction: expose an authenticated read-only startup/recovery progress channel independent of mutation readiness and prove durable recovery transitions at actual effect/context owners. Preserve fail-closed mutation admission and exact phase ordering. No tests or formal verification run.

### L784 — TUI composition duplicates whole drafts before its fixed task-size rejection

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/input/composer.rs:1-187`, `input/selection.rs:1-50`, `input/output.rs:1-141`, `input/terminal.rs:1-88`, and `model/chat/keys.rs:1-195`, all completely read; crate manifest and README completely read.
- Behavior: Paste filters and allocates the whole incoming text before checking `MAX_PRODUCT_TASK_BYTES`; keyboard insertion stops silently at that same task bound. Composer layout constructs rows, spans, and per-character byte/cell stops for the entire draft, including during vertical movement and mouse hit testing. The one-to-six composer-row clamp and fixed modal geometry are viewport choices, not limits on stored lines. Transcript copying freezes only the visible rows. Control-byte sanitization prevents pasted text from becoming terminal commands, and pasted slash-command tokens require an explicit keyboard intent.
- Consequence: The fixed protocol task cap still prevents a larger daily-driving instruction from being entered, while a maximum-size draft/paste can consume substantial synchronous UI work before rejection or display. There is no execution timeout in these layout/encoding helpers. Full source reading established the cost pattern, not a measured live freeze.
- Repair direction: Support durable referenced/chunked instructions and viewport-local layout; enforce negotiated inline capacity before unnecessary copying. Preserve UTF-8 boundaries, terminal sanitization, and explicit command intent.

### L785 — Chat progress is gated by volatile pending lookups and a missing binding can detach the run

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat.rs:1-299`, `model/chat/binding.rs:1-145`, and `model/chat/commands.rs:1-218`, completely read.
- Behavior: A pending chat query, open, binding, or product-message binding suppresses all `poll_chat` work, including the goal poll. Submission and model changes wait for volatile mutation/binding bookkeeping. The first send on an unchecked saved run performs a binding lookup and requires the user to send again. If a run remains selected without a durable workbench destination after that path, sending clears the run/binding and asks for another Enter to start a new conversation. Binding depends on negotiated `WorkbenchRunBinding`. Opening another workspace also blocks on an unsent draft; active mode changes require an explicit stop. Command dispatch closes the file panel before it validates the command and generally leaves goal-inspection mode for unrelated commands.
- Consequence: A slow/unresolved lookup can suppress visible progress even though daemon work continues. The detach/new-conversation fallback can make an unavailable original destination look like ephemeral session behavior; it does not recover the original native context. Mutation serialization and exact workspace routing protect authority and need durable reconciliation rather than deletion. The current live session's lockup was not reproduced by this source read.
- Repair direction: Separate independent observation streams, preserve the original durable run/destination through lookup failure, and expose reconciliation state with a retry that retains identity. Trace pending-request expiration and reconnect ownership in the runtime and receipt handlers.

### L786 — Selection overlays consume control keys, and model updates clear intent before send success

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/navigation.rs:1-258`, `model/chat/doctor.rs:1-99`, `model/chat/picker.rs:1-34`, `model/chat/models.rs:1-305`, `model/chat/models/effort.rs:1-92`, `model/chat/working.rs:1-70`, `model/chat/catalog.rs:1-214`, and `model/chat/catalog/entries.rs:1-264`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Terminal-selection mode handles every key before chat control routing and consumes it until Esc/F2 or paste restores live mode; Ctrl-R and normal quit/cancel keys therefore do not reach their usual handlers while it owns input. Clipboard copying has one pending operation per selection. Doctor and model discovery deduplicate pending reads, with Esc removing their local request tracking. Manual model IDs bypass catalog membership explicitly; effort choice does not require discovery. Saving model/effort clears the command and closes pickers before `request` can fail to send; a no-run selection exists only in the current UI model. The working indicator resets by busy period/run and only reports elapsed observation time, with no deadline or stop condition.
- Consequence: An input-owner mode can resemble an unresponsive UI; its release is a local mode transition, not provider reconnection. An offline/failed model update requires reconstructing the cleared intent, and process restart loses unsent UI-only selection. The busy timer is not an artificial execution limiter. No live UI or tests were exercised in this audit.
- Repair direction: Make input ownership and release continuously visible, preserve exact model-update intent until durable acknowledgement, and reconcile it through reconnect. Keep explicit manual-ID/command boundaries and observer-only elapsed accounting.

### L787 — The composer accepts a larger draft than durable chat admission can represent

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/conversation.rs:1-338` and `sessions.rs:1-147`, completely read; task-sized editing gate in L784.
- Behavior: Normal chat admission converts the entire draft to `WorkbenchInputText` and rejects anything outside 1–8,192 bytes. The composer instead permits `MAX_PRODUCT_TASK_BYTES`. Sending then stages creation, queue admission, execution discovery/start, and continuation through separate receipts. New titles are derived from at most 64 characters; explicit session titles and literal searches are capped at 256 bytes, and library requests ask for 64 rows with pagination. An archived session requires explicit unarchive. The continuation command has no independent operation identity, as recorded in L716.
- Consequence: A valid editable draft can become unsendable at Enter. A queued input can survive while later execution admission fails or remains unresolved; the UI cannot infer that receipt acceptance means the original native window was recovered. Title/search page capacities differ from execution budgets and authority checks must remain explicit.
- Repair direction: Unify the editable/admitted input contract using durable referenced text, and make queue-to-execution continuation an idempotent operation with a recoverable worker identity. Preserve archive, workspace, and user-stop authority.

### L788 — Exact control recovery exists only in the retained UI model, and some messages overstate admission

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench.rs:1-394`, `refresh.rs:1-96`, `receipts.rs:1-341`, `receipts/correlation.rs:1-40`, `receipts/recovery.rs:1-37`, `receipts/rejection.rs:1-54`, and `receipts/error.rs:1-236`, all completely read. Response callers `src/model/protocol/response.rs:1-383` and `response/control.rs:1-187` were fully reread.
- Behavior: An original workbench command and draft are retained in `WorkbenchUi.unresolved`; reconnect queries that exact operation before explicit replay. Receipt matching checks operation, destination, and accepted revision. For ResumeGoal, a read-only recovered receipt deliberately leaves the operation unresolved and requires `/sessions retry` because worker launch is separately persisted. Ordinary review receipts label explanation/revision work as started, although the admission/launch split in L753 can prevent execution. Most panel error state uses only the error code rather than diagnostic/recovery detail. A normal disconnect clears pending request maps but retains this command only in the process-local model.
- Consequence: This is stronger than creating a new operation on reconnect, but it is not a durable client outbox that survives loss of the UI process. A missing launch or receipt may fence later edits indefinitely; a claimed start can obscure that distinction. Exact receipt and consent fencing should remain, while recovery must identify accepted-but-unlaunched work.
- Repair direction: Persist client intents and their settlement state, bind launch reconciliation to the accepted operation, and report admission separately from observed launch. Surface the retained diagnostic/recovery source without replacing uncertain operations by new identities.

### L789 — Removing request expiry left global pending-read gates without independent progress recovery

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/navigation.rs:1-181`, `navigation/cancel.rs:1-80`, and `tests/timeouts.rs:1-99`, completely read. `src/model.rs:1-607`, `src/model/protocol.rs:1-305`, `src/model/product/observation.rs:1-153`, and `src/runtime.rs:1-347` were fully reread to trace the caller path.
- Behavior: The current reducer does not expire requests by elapsed ticks. The timeout-named tests explicitly advance to tick 10,000 and require slow reads/model updates to remain pending. `workbench_request_pending` globally combines local file/image reading with virtually every workbench query, receipt, mutation, and preview lookup. Refresh and new chat admission return without sending while any such item is pending. Esc abandons ordinary inspection tracking, but if a chat submission or unresolved mutation exists it retains the entire workflow; reconnect clears transport requests and re-queries the same retained receipt. Slow recent/exact run queries suppress dashboard polls, while chat and preview polling run before that dashboard gate. Chat itself still has the lookup gate in L785.
- Consequence: A never-returning read or reconciliation step can permanently block independent controls despite the removal of artificial deadlines. The tests establish absence of time-based disconnection, not eventual progress, cancellation of the host operation, or native recovery. The README still describes read-only request timeouts/expiry, which does not match this current reducer.
- Repair direction: Give independent observations independently supersedable ownership, provide cancellation/reconciliation transitions for pending operations, and preserve accepted-mutation identities through durable recovery. Do not substitute another execution deadline for these missing transitions. No tests were run.

### L790 — Canceling an attachment panel does not cancel its capacity-one blocking file reader

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/files.rs:1-40`, `runtime/images.rs:1-32`, `runtime/interrupts.rs:1-36`, and `runtime/product.rs:1-190`, completely read; runtime dispatch fully reread as cited in L789.
- Behavior: File and image readers each admit one `spawn_blocking` job until their JoinSet produces a completion. Panel dismissal changes reducer ownership and suppresses late continuation, but these reader APIs have no cancellation operation. A second read reports that another read is still finishing. Thread work uses the existing synchronous whole-source readers (L261) and remains active through a stuck filesystem read. The event loop otherwise selects local job completions alongside input, connection, ticks, and process interrupts. Product launch facts scope run/conversation/latest selection to the caller's workspace; they are not fresh health evidence.
- Consequence: A slow or stuck old read can prevent a new explicit attachment read after its panel was dismissed. It does not by itself stop daemon work, and introducing a timer would not cancel a blocking filesystem thread or make effects recoverable.
- Repair direction: Implement cancellable/chunked reads with independently owned reader generations and explicit completion settlement; permit unrelated requests to progress without falsely claiming the old job stopped.

### L791 — Foreground candidate execution suspends the whole UI reducer without a durable process owner

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/candidate.rs:1-144`, `candidate/foreground.rs:1-152`, and `runtime/terminal.rs:1-221`, all completely read; caller `src/runtime.rs:1-347` fully reread.
- Behavior: Running a candidate checks the exact repository digest, parses a direct executable/argument command, stops the terminal input worker, suspends the full-screen terminal, and awaits a blocking child-status task. That await does not pump `next_effects`, daemon events, subscription acknowledgements, local reads, or model polls. Interrupt signals are consumed while waiting for the foreground command to exit. Unix transfers the terminal to the child's process group, observes stops with waitpid, and waits for shell SIGCONT before foreground restoration; handoff failure kills that group. This child has no durable C2 launch receipt or reconnect/adoption identity here. The 100 ms input poll/park is a scheduling cadence, not a lifetime cap; selection mode deliberately skips all subsequent redraws until release.
- Consequence: A long-running or interrupt-resistant candidate can keep the interface unavailable while its connection event queue stops draining; loss of the owning client cannot adopt this same process through these APIs. Natural command duration and OS job-control waits must not be replaced by a synthetic execution deadline. Candidate digest/foreground ownership checks are integrity boundaries.
- Repair direction: Keep connection/control progress alive during terminal handoff and route candidate launches through a durable process owner with explicit cancel, exit, and adoption receipts. Preserve correct foreground process groups and exact candidate authorization.

### L792 — Clipboard writing has no default deadline but a hung helper holds its sole slot

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/clipboard.rs:1-216`, completely read.
- Behavior: Production clipboard copy passes `None` to the optional native-helper timeout. The 100 ms/one-second deadlines appear only in tests that deliberately select a timeout. The writer permits one pending job; it sends all text to wl-copy/xclip/pbcopy, closes stdin, and waits for exit. Only a missing helper falls back to OSC 52; other helper errors are returned. The fallback synchronously writes and flushes terminal stdout from the async task. kill-on-drop covers the immediate helper, without a durable owned-process record or explicit in-UI cancel API.
- Consequence: A stalled helper occupies the copy slot until completion/drop, and a blocked fallback terminal write can stall the runtime. There is no artificial production clipboard deadline to remove. Whole selection encoding and stdout work are not progress-aware.
- Repair direction: Provide an owned, cancellable clipboard operation and avoid blocking the UI executor on terminal transport; retain exact inert Unicode bytes and truthful failure/acknowledgement reporting.

### L794 — A stale compaction preview is refreshed with the same obsolete revision

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/compaction.rs:1-117`, `context.rs:1-176`, and `brief.rs:1-163`, completely read; stale snapshot refresh scope and inspection error handlers in L788.
- Behavior: `/compact` builds its request from the retained conversation snapshot; `refresh_compaction` clones that exact stored request. On compaction inspection failure, the error handler clears the preview but leaves both request and conversation snapshot. Automatic checkpoints can advance the aggregate revision without a UI mutation receipt. General pre-command snapshot refresh handles checkpoint/rewind/fork and selected session metadata actions, but not compaction. Therefore pressing refresh can repeatedly query the same obsolete revision until the operator separately refreshes the conversation. Context/queue pages have explicit revision and offset validation, while brief edits require exact inspected proposal identity. Compaction focus is limited to 1,024 bytes and brief text to 8,192 bytes.
- Consequence: This is a state-refresh loop rather than an elapsed-time failure. Exact revision/consent checks prevent applying an obsolete preview and must remain. Context inspection displays metadata and does not reconnect a provider window.
- Repair direction: On an obsolete preview request, obtain a fresh aggregate snapshot, rebuild a newly inspectable preview, and require confirmation of that new preview. Preserve the original draft and source intent; do not replay a previously consented mutation against changed contents.

### L795 — Queue reorder requires every pending ID but the composer cannot hold the largest valid order

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/queue.rs:1-257`, `library.rs:1-133`, and `fork.rs:1-106`, completely read; larger fixed queue/domain bounds in L705 and composer bound in L784.
- Behavior: Reorder accepts one textual list containing all pending 32-hex IDs and constructs the whole vector before the input-order validator. The protocol admits up to 65,535 IDs, requiring about 2.16 MiB of textual identifiers and separators, beyond the 1 MiB composer task bound. Queue text itself remains capped at 8,192 bytes. Paged row selection preserves exact input revision/identity, and aggregate refresh does not reinterpret an old row against a reordered list. Library navigation is paged; fork requires exact checkpoint references and truncates only the generated title at a UTF-8 boundary.
- Consequence: The UI cannot express a valid maximum-size reorder even though the underlying order type accepts it. Page sizes/title presentation do not end execution. Immutable row/checkpoint/workspace checks are authority boundaries, not synthetic runtime ceilings.
- Repair direction: Represent reorder as durable incremental moves or an uploaded/reference-backed exact order, with a revision fence and completion receipt. Retain identity-based selection and independently progressing page reads.

### L796 — Goal drafting is local and goal controls inherit the global read fence

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/goal.rs:1-282`, `goal/draft.rs:1-161`, and `goal/refresh.rs:1-31`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Objectives and graphical criterion descriptions are limited to 8,192 bytes. An unconfirmed draft resides only in WorkbenchUi, permits one optional graphical criterion, and always includes the existing mandatory runner-acceptance criterion. Confirming first saves the exact objective in the brief, then starts the goal after a separately correlated brief refresh. Pause/resume refuse to send while any global workbench request or unresolved command is pending; missing goal inspection asks the user to repeat the control after reading. A refreshed control is retained only while goal identity and draft still match. There is no time, token, turn, or tool budget in these UI goal constructors.
- Consequence: A pending unrelated read can delay even an explicit goal pause/resume, and loss of the UI can lose the unconfirmed draft or the next stage of confirmation. Mandatory acceptance criteria describe completion authority; they are distinct from a synthetic lifetime cap. A native-context recovery guarantee still requires the durable execution-owner work recorded earlier.
- Repair direction: Make explicit goal controls independently admissible against the exact goal identity, persist unconfirmed/partially confirmed user intent, and settle staged brief/goal admission durably. Keep user confirmation, safe-boundary pause semantics, and exact criterion identity.

### L797 — Restore recovery receipts release the UI's exact-operation retry record

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/checkpoints.rs:1-290`, `checkpoints/receipts.rs:1-161`, `memory.rs:1-279`, `permissions.rs:1-158`, and `init.rs:1-137`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Checkpoint/restore matching retains exact operation, checkpoint, destination, revision, and original command. Rewind refresh obtains a fresh snapshot and builds another inspectable preview, unlike compaction in L794. After any matching restore receipt, including RecoveryRequired, `clear_checkpoint_command` takes the unresolved command; the UI clears the rewind request/preview and retains only the restore receipt with instructions to inspect recovery. `/sessions retry` can no longer replay that removed original command through this record. Checkpoint names are capped at 256 bytes. Guidance mutations select only an active ID in the current page and fence both record/dependency/conversation revisions. Permissions intersect immutable host authority, and init requires exact equality to the reviewed proposal.
- Consequence: Durable server history survives, but client retry ownership ends before restore recovery is settled. An operator receives an instruction rather than an executable reconciliation transition. Guidance paging and permission/proposal checks protect user scope and should remain; none of these files adds an execution timer.
- Repair direction: Retain a durable recovery operation until the restore transaction settles, expose its actual reconciliation action, and distinguish accepted recovery state from completed effect. Preserve exact preimages, proposal consent, forget semantics, and host authority.

### L798 — Attachment previews select launcher role defaults instead of the active conversation's provider

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/images.rs:1-245`, `files.rs:1-341`, and `files/import.rs:1-300`, all completely read; `src/model/chat.rs:278-284` and binding/receipt callers already fully read.
- Behavior: Image reads, workspace-file previews, external-text imports, and their confirmation checks take the writer profile from `ProductUi::providers`, which represents the launcher's next-run role selection. Ordinary chat uses `chat_providers`, which first prefers the selected run snapshot's actual providers. Attachment model choice is separately taken from `chat.models.writer`. Thus opening an existing conversation with a different provider can pair its model with the launcher's default profile for preview/consent. Confirmation consistently checks that same launcher profile, rather than resolving the conversation's authoritative provider.
- Consequence: A daily-driving attachment can be rejected by an unrelated default profile's model/media capabilities, or inspected against the wrong provider selection. The exact consent checks themselves are necessary; their source of identity must be corrected. This source-derived mismatch was not reproduced against the installed daemon.
- Repair direction: Resolve provider/model selection through the same exact conversation/run binding used for chat, and invalidate a preview only when that authoritative binding changes. Keep byte digest, workspace, model, and user-confirmation identity together.

### L799 — Attachment upload offsets are acknowledgement-driven but discarded on reconnect

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/images/upload.rs:1-201`, `images/page.rs:1-121`, and `files/import.rs:1-300`, all completely read, together with the attachment parents in L798.
- Behavior: The UI reads selected content into memory, uploads at most 64 KiB per chunk (also respecting negotiated capacity), and advances only after the matching transfer/step acknowledgement. Upload identity, bytes, and next offset live in WorkbenchUi. Interrupt handlers take/drop the upload and request state on disconnect; reconnect asks the user to explicitly preview again rather than querying a persisted accepted offset. Failed chunk construction also drops upload state. Ordinary panel dismissal can send explicit transfer cancellation, but dropping import state is not itself a durable host cancellation receipt. A missing ACK remains behind the global workbench pending gate in L789. Attachment histories use pages rather than an execution lifetime limit.
- Consequence: A transfer interruption can force another whole read/upload with fresh identities and can strand unrelated controls until the pending ownership changes. Chunking here does not establish resumable transfer after UI/daemon replacement. There is no default per-upload time deadline to remove.
- Repair direction: Persist transfer identity/digest and acknowledged offsets, query host settlement after reconnect, and resume/cancel that exact transfer before allocating a replacement. Allow unrelated observation/control channels to progress independently.

### L800 — Caption edits unnecessarily invalidate file previews, and multiline captions are rejected

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/files/keys.rs:1-126`, `files.rs:161-295`, `files/import.rs:71-94,222-279`, and `images/editor.rs:1-97`, all completely read.
- Behavior: File field editing calls `discard_preview` after every editor key, including caption changes and cursor movement. A user who previews first, then enters the required caption, must preview/read again before confirmation. Image caption editing does not discard its byte preview. Both caption editors reject every Unicode control character on paste, including newline/tab, despite WorkbenchInputText supporting ordinary multiline text and the README promising multiline captions. Field limits are 4,096 path bytes, 80 file-range bytes, and 8,192 caption bytes. File preview/read acceptance checks destination and path but does not compare the current range/refresh draft to the request's range/refresh when an already-issued reply arrives.
- Consequence: The file workflow can induce repeated reads without acceptance and can reject a normal pasted multiline instruction. An old range reply can become available after the range draft changed, although confirmation still carries the preview's exact original request. This is a UI state/consent mismatch, not a provider execution timeout.
- Repair direction: Keep byte-preview consent stable across caption/cursor edits, allow inert newline/tab in caption text, and correlate incoming previews with the full current source/range/mode generation. Repreview only when bytes, selection, or authoritative provider binding changes.

### L801 — TUI rendering processes whole retained content before taking visible rows

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/render/chat.rs:1-285`, `chat/transcript.rs:1-171`, `chat/inspector.rs:1-89`, `chat/doctor.rs:1-100`, `editor.rs:1-147`, and every workbench content renderer receipted in this batch, all completely read.
- Behavior: Each transcript draw sanitizes and wraps every retained activity before selecting the viewport. Tool rows are fully built/wrapped before the collapsed view keeps three opening and three final rows and inserts an explicit omission marker. Composer/modal/image editors lay out the entire draft before selecting visible rows. Inspector draw and scroll-limit calculation each build all content lines and wrap them; library selection also rebuilds its preceding items. Doctor chains fresh daemon findings with the launcher's retained report and rebuilds the combined text. Goal criteria, checkpoint paths/exclusions, briefs, and other already-bounded payloads are likewise expanded into whole display vectors.
- Consequence: A small viewport does not bound synchronous formatting/allocation work. Frequent tick/event redraws can become expensive for large valid snapshots, even when middle tool output is hidden. This is a source-derived cost pattern, not a measured freeze in the original running instance. Collapsed previews and viewport geometry do not terminate daemon execution.
- Repair direction: Cache immutable formatted generations and virtualize rows/content so redraw and navigation cost follow the visible region. Keep exact source references and explicit omission markers; fetch historical pages rather than requiring a whole transcript to render first.

### L802 — Some display bounds can hide recovery details or omit wide characters

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/render/prompts.rs:1-141`, `chat/transcript.rs:134-170`, `status.rs:1-82`, `tabs.rs:1-81`, and `chat/status.rs:1-51`, all completely read; additional content renderers in this batch completely read.
- Behavior: Prompt scrolling uses u16 offsets and saturates its maximum at 65,535 wrapped rows, unlike the workbench inspector's usize row slicing. Transcript wrapping skips a grapheme whose cell width exceeds the available width; at width one a wide character can disappear from visible/copyable rows. General status uses a single unwrapped line, while chat uses two unwrapped lines, so long recovery messages are clipped by terminal width. RecoveryRequired always advertises `/retry` without consulting the operation's legal-control set; the control handler can then refuse that action. Queue previews disclose their three-line/160-character truncation and offer exact full-text inspection, while briefs disclose the existing eight-proposal/8,192-byte exclusions. These are presentation/input-access boundaries, not execution deadlines.
- Consequence: A narrow display can obscure the cause/action needed to leave a blocked state, and sufficiently long valid prompt projections would outgrow the scroll representation. A displayed retry hint does not prove that a recovery transition is legal or executable. None of these findings establishes the current live lockup by itself.
- Repair direction: Use addressable row paging/usize navigation, preserve indivisible wide graphemes through resizing, and derive visible recovery actions from the same legal-control/reconciliation state as dispatch. Keep exact authority IDs and distinguish observed accounting from unavailable provider counters.

### L805 — Web operation capacity can be consumed forever by already reconciled transport children

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/state.rs:17,261-298`; `src/daemon/receipts.rs:253-345`, `src/operations.rs:13-75`, `src/files/edit.rs:46-85` in that crate.
- Behavior: the ledger admits at most 4,096 records when no completed record is removable; completed eviction follows BTreeMap identity order. Generic postcondition recovery returns a successful observation and stores the parent result, but does not complete its native transport record. Those unresolved children are hidden from the pending-operation list and are removed only by manual review, which returns early if the parent already has a result. File saves bypass the admission guard by directly inserting records.
- Consequence: recoveries can accumulate invisible unresolved children until new actions are refused. Completed receipt eviction also removes the persisted deduplication basis for a previously used operation identity. A file-save bypass can enlarge a fully unresolved ledger further. These are count-based synthetic admission and retention bounds, not timeouts. Source-derived; not reproduced against the installed gateway.
- Repair direction: atomically settle parent and transport disposition on proved recovery, retain durable identity tombstones independent of display history, and separate paging/storage policy from action admission.

### L806 — Web stop shares the send wait, while supposedly observational recovery can start execution

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/api.rs:100-168,181-214`; `src/operations.rs:13-60`, `src/daemon/chat.rs:35-65,67-201`, `src/daemon/receipts.rs:66-115,139-177,223-251` in that crate.
- Behavior: send, control and model settings take the same conversation mutex for the entire awaited request pipeline. A missing reply holds it indefinitely; stop waits behind send. GET operation observation invokes recover_send, which drives create/queue/start/continuation and can retransmit an exact domain command. Observation does not take the operation/conversation guards used by mutations; manual acknowledgement calls observation first.
- Consequence: a stalled submission can prevent cancellation through the same UI, and polling or review of an uncertain operation can cause execution rather than merely report its disposition. Concurrent recovery observes may race. Exact domain identities reduce duplicate effects but do not make this a read-only operation or prove native ownership recovery. Removing a timer alone leaves the shared-control blocker.
- Repair direction: give controls and receipt inspection independent access to the owning operation, make observation read-only, and route explicitly authorized resume through serialized durable operation state. Preserve unknown-effect and exact-command fences.

### L807 — Web attachments are accepted at sizes that the durable message cannot send

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/files/attachments.rs:28-111`; `src/daemon/chat.rs:14-33` in that crate.
- Behavior: staging accepts text snapshots up to 48 KiB and up to 16 selections; its error promises a 64 KiB combined message limit. Sending embeds all selected content and metadata as JSON, then rejects the complete message above 8 KiB. A separate 256 MiB retained-attachment metadata quota has no removal action in the fully read API dispatcher; deleting bytes alone does not remove the metadata sum.
- Consequence: valid staged attachments, including a single large snapshot, become unsendable; encoding/metadata further reduce usable text capacity. Normal repeated attachment use can reach a permanent cache-admission blocker. Exact source/session/digest checks are integrity requirements, not synthetic lifecycle limits.
- Repair direction: use durable attachment handles and chunked source admission consistently with the daemon, disclose the actual assembled capacity before accepting selections, and provide explicit durable snapshot removal/storage reconciliation.

### L808 — Web consoles are process-local and counted even after the CLI exits

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/terminal.rs:29-131`; `src/state.rs:55-62,114-120`, `src/consoles.rs:19-88`, `src/api.rs:307-310,357-389` in that crate.
- Behavior: the gateway stores only in-memory PTY owners and refuses the 25th console even if existing children have ended. Output beyond 1 MiB is discarded with an explicit lost-offset flag, delivered in 64 KiB pages. CLI arguments cap at 128 and 32,768 bytes each; terminal input caps at 65,536 bytes and geometry at 10–400 columns/2–200 rows. Drop kills and waits for the direct child synchronously, with no owned persistent adopt record or joined reader thread.
- Consequence: gateway exit discards console identities and output and terminates CLI children on ordinary Drop; a restarted gateway starts with an empty map. Finished consoles consume capacity until explicitly closed. A blocked input write or child wait can hold an async handler or the consoles map lock indefinitely. Retaining a map entry during one gateway lifetime is not persistent session ownership.
- Repair direction: separate display subscriptions from durable process ownership, persist console binding/output offsets with explicit close disposition, and make child/group lifecycle and input waits observable and cancelable without expiration.

### L809 — Web state schema failure becomes a fresh workspace, and receipt replacement lacks directory durability

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/state.rs:19-54,77-125,127-149,223-257,300-351`.
- Behavior: any workspace JSON deserialization failure, including unknown fields, invokes best-effort quarantine and then uses an empty workspace even if quarantine failed. The schema has no versioned migration. save syncs the temporary file before replacement but does not sync the parent directory; every update clones and pretty-serializes all projects, sessions, receipts and attachments while holding one mutex. Nesting traverses ancestor links without a visited set for a preexisting persisted cycle.
- Consequence: incompatible/corrupt metadata can silently detach saved session/operation ownership and seed a new conversation; subsequent saves may replace state after a failed quarantine. Crash durability of the renamed receipt is not established by file sync alone. Long histories and preexisting lineage cycles can stall shared state access. Source-derived; no power-loss or malformed-cycle experiment run.
- Repair direction: version and migrate state explicitly, preserve incompatible originals and unresolved identities without fresh-state substitution, durably sync replacements, page records independently, and validate lineage on load.

### L810 — Web daemon discovery and request sessions do not preserve a native owner binding

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/daemon.rs:29-112,134-149,194-261,281-323`; `src/daemon/receipts.rs:24-44,223-236`, `src/sessions.rs:97-212`, `src/daemon/readiness.rs:8-88` in that crate.
- Behavior: configuration and product snapshots are selected separately by lexicographically last filename, without binding the selected product state to the config/store. Every raw request and retry opens a new Client with no retained app SessionId; the prepared message retains conversation/run/workspace/provider/model/text but not endpoint/store/native process ownership. Opening a run requires an already-open project whose separately discovered facts match. Doctor checks current admission and explicitly defers authentication until use.
- Consequence: stored browser sessions are persistent presentation identities, while connections and endpoint discovery can change independently. They do not establish continuity of an active native provider window, and discovery failure can force setup or project reopening despite retained daemon work. Transport sessions must not be confused with provider context windows. No live-instance reproduction is claimed.
- Repair direction: bind durable browser operations and discovery to explicit store/workspace/endpoint ownership, reconcile that binding on restart, and qualify native context adoption separately from metadata reopening.

### L811 — Web paging and Git actions still wait for whole-content work

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/files.rs:17-43,61-95`; `src/daemon.rs:372-392`, `src/git.rs:13-80,81-125`, `src/git/workflows.rs:8-47`, `src/api.rs:181-214` in that crate.
- Behavior: directory pages collect/stat/sort the entire directory before selecting 250 entries; text previews fully read/hash up to 50 MiB. Run listing aggregates every daemon page before returning HTTP data; refs/remotes inventory runs sequential whole-output Git commands. Git output waits without a deadline under the project mutation lock, with kill_on_drop only for the direct child and no cancellation route for the owning operation.
- Consequence: pagination does not bound work done per response. Large histories/output and stalled hooks/signers/network children can make UI requests appear locked and prevent same-target actions indefinitely. Natural external readiness/integrity failures and ordinary Git dirty-worktree protections must remain explicit; adding a blanket timeout would not repair ownership.
- Repair direction: expose durable cursors and incremental result work, and own native Git effects with observable lifecycle, independent controls and reconciliation of uncertain outcomes.

### L812 — Web presentation and HTTP bounds are separate from execution lifetime

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/config.rs:174-209`; `src/api.rs:25-41,130-140,224-244,315-350`, `src/files/pdf.rs:6-25`, `src/consoles.rs:53-69` in that crate.
- Behavior: HTTP bodies cap at 4 MiB except the 50 MiB file-save route; operation IDs cap at 80 ASCII characters. Preferences accept font sizes 12–22, explorer widths 180–480, three themes, two densities and at most 100 aliases/shortcuts. Renamed titles cap at 256 bytes although the error says characters; new-session titles are not validated until the later daemon preparation. PDF identification inspects the first 1,024 bytes and downloads remain available. Console display titles/suggestions cap at 120 characters/32,768 bytes.
- Consequence: these are representation/admission bounds, not run TTLs. The inconsistent title validation allows a locally created session that later cannot prepare a daemon conversation; configurable alias count and fixed dimensions can also refuse ordinary customization. Loopback origin/token checks, literal path confinement and invalid command rejection protect authority and should not be removed as timers.
- Repair direction: use one validated title contract at creation/edit/preparation, document actual representation units, and make presentation/storage bounds adaptable without ending owned work. No tests were run during this source audit.

### L814 — Browser startup and polling can wait forever while recovery controls are hidden

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/workspace.svelte.ts:42-70`, `117-180`, `235-252`; `webui/src/App.svelte:58-63`; `webui/src/lib/components/Recovery.svelte:1-21`; `webui/src/lib/components/FileViewer.svelte:1-89`.
- Behavior: Startup awaits refresh, project Git/facts, poll, and operation reconciliation before releasing its loading gate. Each poll awaits status, consoles, facts, and every pending operation before refreshing conversations. The next timer is scheduled only after completion. Recovery controls hide during pending send/attachment or any Git action, and a pending check/save retains its disabled state until the response returns.
- Consequence: One unresolved request can prevent conversation refresh, startup completion, or recovery access indefinitely. Removing timeouts does not provide independently owned cancellation, progress, or recovery. The 3500-ms refresh cadence is not a session deadline. This is source-derived; browser lockup has not been measured in this audit.
- Repair direction: Make observations independent, retain durable effect identities, provide controls that remain reachable while an effect is unresolved, and let cancellation/reconciliation operate independently of the original request. Do not restore an arbitrary execution deadline. No tests run.

### L815 — Browser recovery promises do not match recovery effects or persistence

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/api.ts:1-62`; `webui/src/lib/operations.svelte.ts:1-16`; `webui/src/lib/files/drafts.svelte.ts:1-33`; `webui/src/lib/workspace.svelte.ts:161-180`; `webui/src/lib/components/Recovery.svelte:7-18`; gateway mutation evidence L806.
- Behavior: Recovery messaging says nothing is repeated and that review only clears the receipt, while the queried gateway recovery path can transmit commands and start execution before acknowledgement. The browser stores operation identifiers and metadata in sessionStorage, not the original executable payload; file drafts and save snapshots exist only in module memory. Best-effort storage writes can fail silently, and sessionStorage enumeration is outside the restore catch.
- Consequence: A user cannot rely on the advertised observational boundary, tab/crash continuity, or survival of an unresolved edit. A denied storage read can itself interrupt startup. Chat draft localStorage persistence is separate and does not make file drafts or native context durable.
- Repair direction: Separate receipt inspection, explicit retry, and acknowledgement into distinct effects; persist exact unresolved payloads and file drafts under stable workspace/session identities, and surface storage failure. Preserve the rule against repeating an ambiguous effect without its original identity. No tests run.

### L816 — Browser console interruption shares an unresolved input queue

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Console.svelte:1-41`; process-local gateway console and output limits in L808.
- Behavior: Console input, including Ctrl-C bytes, is chained behind previous input promises. The input field clears before acknowledgement without a durable original. Terminal scrollback is 4000 lines. A new component starts reading at offset zero, and each next read waits for the previous request before applying its 250-ms or 1800-ms cadence.
- Consequence: An unresolved input request can prevent the later interrupt from reaching the process. Browser history and the gateway's 1-MiB output ring are separate eviction boundaries; the 64-KiB page and polling cadence can lose output when production outruns retrieval. Closing a panel does not transfer native process ownership or preserve its output. Cadences are not execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: Give interruption an independent owner/control path, retain input effect receipts, and use durable output with acknowledged offsets rather than relying on process-local rings and browser scrollback. No tests run.

### L817 — Activity ordering can discard authoritative state, and control replies can move between sessions

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/conversations.ts:1-10`; `webui/src/lib/workspace.svelte.ts:235-236`.
- Behavior: The merge guard compares activity-tail identifiers and rejects the whole incoming conversation if its tail is older, including incoming phase and legal controls. Control dispatch sends the selected session identity before awaiting the action, then reevaluates the current selected identity when assigning its response.
- Consequence: Truncated or older activity snapshots can hide newer recovery/cancel/model state. Switching selection while a control request is pending can assign the old session's returned conversation to the new session. These are state-authority/identity errors, not legitimate lifetime limits.
- Repair direction: Merge authoritative fields by their own revisions, keep activity ordering local to activity data, and capture the destination identity across every asynchronous effect. No tests run.

### L818 — Alias depth and editor undo impose additional synthetic boundaries

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/workspace.svelte.ts:207-210`; `webui/src/lib/components/TextEditor.svelte:1-84`.
- Behavior: Alias dispatch declares a cycle once recursion exceeds eight even for an acyclic chain. Editor undo keeps at most 200 changes and 2000000 cumulative UTF-16 units; trimming can remove a single newly added edit that exceeds that budget. Undo history belongs to the mounted component and is lost on remount.
- Consequence: Valid long alias chains fail, and a sufficiently large accepted paste can have no immediate undo. These are command-graph and editing limits, separate from provider capacity or session lifetime.
- Repair direction: Detect repeated alias identities rather than counting valid expansions, and preserve reversible edits through stable draft-owned history or durable deltas with explicit user-controlled retention. No tests run.

### L819 — Browser improvement capacity claims and text counters disagree with daemon admission

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Improvements.svelte:1-52`; `webui/src/lib/components/Overlays.svelte:1-49`; actual improvement capacity evidence L699 and web text admission L812.
- Behavior: The improvements view announces a full inbox at 32 although the audited daemon capacity is 65535. Its textarea maxlength is 4096 JavaScript units while daemon admission counts 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Session title editing similarly permits 256 units against a 256-byte backend value. The composer has no equivalent preflight for its smaller durable message bound (L807).
- Consequence: The interface can falsely report capacity exhaustion or accept input that is rejected only after submission, especially non-ASCII text. These stale presentation/admission limits do not prove a runtime deadline.
- Repair direction: Derive visible capacity and validation from the authoritative schema and validate the exact encoded value while preserving drafts and unresolved effects. No tests run.

### L820 — Frontend paging does not bound whole-content work or preserve all editor state

- Evidence: `webui/src/App.svelte:1-181`; `webui/src/lib/components/Markdown.svelte:1-13`; `webui/src/lib/components/Overlays.svelte:1-49`; `webui/src/lib/components/TextEditor.svelte:1-84`; `webui/src/lib/files/text.ts:1-29`; `webui/src/lib/components/FileViewer.svelte:1-89`; `webui/src/lib/components/PdfViewer.svelte:1-33`.
- Behavior: Retained activities and collections are rendered in full; Markdown parsing/sanitization and persistence serialization are synchronous. File paging at 128000 UTF-16 units follows a whole-file fetch with original, normalized draft, and snapshot copies; page indexes, cursor positions, searches, and replacements inspect whole text. A page boundary can split a surrogate pair. Stale-result flags suppress rendering but do not cancel requests. Mixed newline editing is deliberately rejected to avoid rewriting format, while edits over 2 MiB use an explicit confirmation rather than a hard block.
- Consequence: Large retained sessions/files can monopolize browser work despite paged display, and abandoned fetches still consume gateway resources. Presentation paging is not durable context recovery. Actual freeze or memory exhaustion has not been measured.
- Repair direction: Preserve stable drafts, incrementally render/index contents, move expensive work off the input path, and cancel obsolete observations through their owners. Keep content-integrity safeguards distinct from arbitrary limits. No tests run.

### L821 — Explorer paging lacks consistent request and directory identities

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Explorer.svelte:1-40`; `webui/src/lib/components/FileNode.svelte:1-30`; whole-directory server work L811.
- Behavior: Root results are guarded only by project identity; concurrent refresh/load-more in the same project can race, and load-more remains available during a request. Child nodes cache results without a project-generation check. Recursive expansion has no canonical directory cycle identity. Filtering searches only pages already loaded.
- Consequence: Duplicate or stale nodes, stale children across project changes, and indefinitely expandable in-project symlink cycles can obstruct navigation. The 250-entry page is not a whole-directory search or a lifetime limit; expansion requires user actions and is not an automatic infinite traversal.
- Repair direction: Bind results to project/directory/query generations, reconcile page identity, and use canonical ancestry to identify cycles while preserving access to legitimate directories. No tests run.

### L823 — Settings save can overwrite edits made while the request is unresolved

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Settings.svelte:6-14`, `19-33`.
- Behavior: Saving disables only the Save button. Preference controls, view switching, import, and Reset remain active. A successful awaited response replaces ui.preferences, ui.config, and the editor source, even when newer edits were made during that request. Reset can submit another mutation while an earlier save remains unresolved. Import reads the whole selected file before gateway admission.
- Consequence: A slow or hung save leaves an unresolved operation without protecting the user's newer configuration draft; a later response can replace it. This is an ownership/revision issue, not a reason to kill the request after an arbitrary duration. Whole-file import also precedes the gateway's action-body bound.
- Repair direction: Capture immutable submitted values and draft revisions, reconcile the response to its original draft, preserve later edits, and give unresolved configuration effects a reachable recovery path. No tests run.

### L857 — Installed service templates impose restart and stop limits

- Source: `packaging/linux/peritus.service:4-13`; `packaging/windows/Peritus.Task.xml.in:20-47`; `packaging/macos/com.corvidae.peritus.plist.in:14-22`.
- Linux permits **five starts within 300 seconds**, restarts failures after **five seconds**, and sets a **40-second stop timeout** with mixed kill mode. Windows has no total execution-time limit (`PT0S`), but allows only **five failure restarts** at five-second intervals and permits hard termination. macOS throttles relaunch to **five seconds** and restarts unsuccessful exits.
- Daily-driving consequence: Linux and Windows can exhaust automatic recovery after repeated daemon failures, leaving reconnection dependent on external intervention. Stop deadlines can also interrupt graceful recovery. These are checked-in templates; installation of these registrations on the original live instance has not been established.
- Repair direction: preserve daemon and task identity through recoverable failures, remove fixed restart exhaustion, and coordinate shutdown with durable recovery receipts. No service or process was changed.

### L858 Upgrades use disposable rollback state and lack a durable session handoff

- Evidence: full `packaging/linux/Upgrade-Peritus.sh`, `packaging/macos/Upgrade-Peritus.sh`, `packaging/windows/Upgrade-Peritus.ps1`; `packaging/linux/Install-Peritus.sh:83-98`; `packaging/macos/Install-Peritus.sh:36-45`; `packaging/windows/Install-Peritus.ps1:90-108`; `packaging/linux/Uninstall-Peritus.sh:17-44`.
- Behavior: all upgrades copy package files into a temporary backup, invoke the installer, then delete the backup on success or rollback handling. Linux suppresses restore-copy failures and still deletes the backup; macOS removes the application tree before restoring; Windows's finally block deletes backup even when restoration throws. These scripts have no persistent transaction journal, startup recovery, or provider/native session handoff. POSIX installers atomically publish individual files but neither coordinate a multi-file version transaction nor stop the running daemon; Windows installation force-stops matching installed processes first. Linux uninstall coordinates only its registered systemd service, then removes package files.
- Consequence: interruption outside trap/exception handling can leave a mixed installed generation, and failed rollback can erase the retained recovery source. Successful POSIX replacement can coexist with an older running executable; Windows replacement can interrupt active sessions without a checkpoint handshake. User data preservation messages do not demonstrate preservation of native ownership or the provider context window.
- Repair direction: persist installation generation and rollback receipts until recovery is verified, and coordinate upgrades through an exact-instance durable checkpoint/reconnect protocol. Preserve backup on failed restoration and resume interrupted publication instead of relying on disposable scope cleanup. Source inspection only; no upgrade, uninstall, or restart executed.
